hypotheses.H-ok: self_noop same top 12/12 (max |dlogit| <= 0.5, bf16 batching); layer0_all_reproduces_source 12/12; >= 15 edited reads/s
hypotheses.H-broken: any self_noop or layer-0 mismatch: hook placement wrong; stop the queue

decision_rule: Pilot proceeds only if self_noop and layer0_all_reproduces_source are 12/12 (summary.json checks).
controls: base patched into base at the middle layer (must be a no-op)
dissoc source patched at every position at layer 0 (must give the source run's own answer)
n: 1 scene per domain at dev e5f0 (12 cases), layers every 8th; competence 2 items per dev file
notes: 0.8B smoke (same commands, BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-0.8b, n=2 per domain, 6 layers) passed 24/24 on both checks, 2376 edited reads in ~26 s.

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_v1.py manifest --set main dev --name d3_competence_27b --limit 100 --why "D3 gate: can the 27B do pointer_v1's RL/DL/RR, every source and each step alone, in chat format?" && uv run python scripts/pointer_v1.py competence --name d3_competence_27b
question: Can Qwen3.6-27B answer pointer_v1's base prompts, the three source prompts (dissoc, same, redigit) and each step alone (cue -> entity; lookup with the entity named / recalled fact), per domain (animals, planets, elements, months), family (RL, DL, RR) and level (main N=5 first 100 per file; dev N=3, N=5, N=5 + 4 filler, 60 per file)?
why_it_matters: Gate for d3_pilot_27b / d3_main_27b. The patching verdicts are only interpretable on items where the model does the lookup and the recall unedited; new domains (planets order, atomic numbers, month numbers) and the card-in-locker wording are untested on the 27B.

hypotheses.H-competent: clean, sources and steps >= 95% in every animals cell (suite_v1 2x2: 99.5-100%); >= 85% (Wilson lower bound) in every other domain x family cell
hypotheses.H-new-domain-fails: some planets/elements/months RR cell < 85%: the recalled fact (order, atomic number, month number) is answered as a word or wrongly; that domain is then dropped from the patching runs
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-competent 0.7; most likely failure RR on months (answers a month name) or planets (ordinal).

decision_rule: A (domain, family) cell enters the patching runs iff its clean Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.85 (suite_v1 rule); eligibility per item = every prompt of the item right (base, dissoc, same, redigit, hop1, hop2). The pilot/main sample scenes eligible in all three families. Report answer read vs greedy agreement (must be >= 99%).
controls: each step alone (hop1 cue -> entity, hop2 lookup / recall): separates composition failures from missing facts
answer read vs 8-token greedy: validates the one-forward read the patching runs use
n: 100 per (domain, family) in main (1200 items) + 60 per (domain, family, level) in dev (2160 items); ~18k prompts
notes: Greedy, no sampling seeds; item seeds are pointer_v1's (main 701, dev 702). Estimate from the 0.8B smoke (1024 prompts, 34 s generate on the A100) does not scale (launch-bound); used suite_v1/exp20-sized runs on the 27B (~2-4 s per batch of 64 x 8 tokens on an A100) -> ~300 batches + reads ~0.5-0.6 h.

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --name d3_pilot_27b --set dev --levels e5f0 --n 15 --layer-step 4 --competence d3_competence_27b --why "D3 pilot (dev split): what RL's question / final / last tokens carry by depth: identity, position or value" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_pilot_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3_pilot_27b
question: On dev items (N=5, four domains), patching the dissoc source's residual into the base at the question tokens, the template after the question (final), the last two tokens (last) or question+final, one layer at a time (every 4th layer) and over the early/mid/transit windows, does the base answer move to the identity, position or value prediction, and at which depth?
why_it_matters: Explains the "around" route (C2: the lens reads RL's bridge but cannot write it). At layers 44-52 copying C's question-token residual flips RL 98-100% while the lens direction flips 0% (EXPERIMENTS rows 27, 52). position => the lookup is steered by a binding/positional pointer the lens cannot express (H-pointer; C2 explained); identity => the bridge's identity (or a lexical key) in a non-lens code (H-word); value => by 44-52 the answer is already fetched, so read-without-write there is a timing effect, not an "around" code (H-value). Sets the windows for d3_main_27b.

hypotheses.H-pointer: RL, final (and last) at the transit window 44-52: position >= 50%, identity <= 20%, value <= 20%; RR position <= 10% (identity >= 50%); DL position >= 50%
hypotheses.H-value: RL final/last transit: value >= 50% (the source's digit, absent from the base)
hypotheses.H-none: RL final transit changes the answer < 20% (would contradict the suite's copy flips; design mismatch)
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior (before any run): question group identity at layers <= 28 under every hypothesis (the cue words are patched); at 44-52 on final/last: value 0.4, position 0.3, identity 0.3. Mixing Mechanisms predicts position mainly for first/last slots and identity (lexical) / reflexive in the middle: reported by slot.

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring). Per cell (family x group x layer/window, dissoc source, pooled over domains, Wilson 95%): interpretable iff 1 - share(none) has lower bound >= 0.20 and the same control's change rate has upper bound <= 0.10 (else "none" / "damage"); verdict X in {identity, position, value} (RR: identity, position) iff X's lower bound exceeds the other two upper bounds and the chance bar (the rand control's upper bound for X; the per-digit context rate); else "mixed". Primary cell: RL, final, transit. The pilot decides nothing by itself: it fixes the main run's layer range (the layers where RL final changes >= 20%) and is reported with its n.
controls: same source (q_s = q_b at the same slot, same digit, rest of the context reshuffled and redigited): every hypothesis predicts the base answer; rules out damage from patching a residual computed on another context
rand: seeded random direction at the dissoc patch's per-position norm: rules out generic disruption picking a context digit (chance bar for identity/position)
other: another domain's item (same family), its residual at the same distance from the prompt end, rescaled to the dissoc norm: realistic-activation null; also probes a domain-general positional code
context digits predicted by no hypothesis (N=5: 2 per item): the per-digit chance rate inside the same runs
base into base at the middle layer (no-op) and layer-0 all-position patch (reproduces the source): hook checks
n: 15 scenes per domain x 4 domains = 60 per family (180 cases), dev e5f0
notes: Reads per case: 3 checks + 16 layers x 4 groups x 2 (dissoc, same) + 8 layers x 4 x 2 (rand, other) + 3 windows x 4 x 2 = 219 -> 39.4k edited reads. Throughput: suite_split map_A8_v1 (27B, faster box) 76.8k reads in 1205 s = 64/s; read_write layers_v1 50k in 571 s = 87/s; the A100 PCIe at ~1/3 of that -> ~22/s -> 30 min + load. Re-size from d3_smoke_27b's measured rate. Pilot items (dev) are never headline items.

examples_command: uv run python scripts/early_push.py examples --name d4_smoke_27b
question: Does every early_push condition (lens / random pushes at r, a, b, nb, d; embedding pushes; C copies; the edited-input patch; the five text edits; O pushes; plain-text loss) run on Qwen3.6-27B with the hook checks passing?
why_it_matters: Fail-fast gate for d4_push_v1 (D4: is the early lens push that flips RL/BL at layers 16-28 an input-word injection or a write of the intermediate? It decides whether layers_v1's "RL is writable early" contradicts C2). Not a result: n=4.

hypotheses.H-code-ok: summary.json diag.max_zero_scale_vs_none_logit == 0.0 over every zero-scale row (the 0.8B smoke gave 0.0 over 1,134 rows); E-cue (the C prompt) gives X's answer on >= 23/24 items and E-name on >= 20/24; the r-subset lens push reproduces read_write layers_v1's role on >= 95% of the shared (item, layer, scale) cells (summary.json replication.role_agreement); examples.json written with 4 groups
hypotheses.H-bug: any check fails or a stage crashes

decision_rule: Run d4_push_v1 only if every H-code-ok check holds. If replication.role_agreement < 0.95, compare the disagreeing rows (bf16 batch-composition noise: the 0.8B none-vs-clean logit diff was up to 0.375) before deciding; otherwise cancel d4_push_v1 and inspect the log.
controls: zero-scale pushes (scale 0, every layer and subset): must leave the logits bit-identical to the unedited row of the same batch
E-cue = the C prompt (eligible items: X's answer by construction): positive control of the edit path
r-subset lens push = read_write layers_v1's exact push on the same items: replication of 35-61% RL flips
random direction at the same per-position norm for every push
n: 4 per family (BL, BR, RL, RR on 4 shared scenes; countries R, B)
notes: Timing: ~270 edited reads per item (zero scale and three embedding scales added) x 24 items = ~6.5k reads; at the ~22 reads/s the other D-jobs assume for the A100 (1/3 of the H200's 64/s in map_A8_v1) ~5 min, + one 27B load (~3 min), + per-item Python/state overhead (~3.6 s/item on the 0.8B smoke, mostly fixed cost) ~1.5 min, + 16 WikiText rows x 31 full-sequence conditions ~1 min. Results: results/early_push/d4_smoke_27b/.

command: S="uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py" && $S map --name d1_smoke_27b --why "D1 27B smoke: every stage end to end on n=4 per family before the main runs" --n 4 --layers 0 16 32 36 40 && $S parts --name d1_smoke_27b_parts --map d1_smoke_27b --why "D1 27B smoke (forced cells)" --force bind_bridge:36 bridge_word:36 question:36 && $S readwrite --name d1_smoke_27b_rw --map d1_smoke_27b --parts d1_smoke_27b_parts --why "D1 27B smoke (forced cells)" --force bind_bridge:36 bridge_word:36 question:36

question: Does every D1 stage (map, parts, readwrite, examples) run end to end on Qwen3.6-27B, with the hook checks passing, before the main runs spend the night's budget?
why_it_matters: Fail-fast gate for d1_map_v1 / d1_parts_v1 / d1_rw_v1 (the D1 test of whether "lookup-used bridges go around the J-space" is a measurement-location artefact). Not a result: n=4, forced cells.

hypotheses.H-code-ok: map sanity: identity copies keep the clean top token in 100% of cases and equal the unedited read in the same batch exactly (|ld difference| = 0; against the separate unedited read only bf16 batch rounding, 0.41 logit on the 0.8B smoke); C copied at every position at layer 0 gives C's top token in >= 31/32 cases; RL/RR/countries-R statement copies have exactly zero delta in every case and layer (zero causality violations) and their reads equal the identity's exactly; read vs greedy >= 99%; BL/BR bridge_word copy at layer 0 flips >= 3/4 cases
hypotheses.H-bug: any of the above fails, or a stage crashes
