controls: identity: AddRows of zero at every position (hook path changes nothing)
all0: C's delta at every position at layer 0 (the copy reproduces C: positive control of the hook)
cue-only families: C's statement copies are exactly zero by causality (checked numerically) and read anyway
O's copy and a random direction at the copy's per-position norms at every map cell
n: 4 per family (BL, BR, RL, RR, BLR, BRL, countries R, B)
notes: Timing: the map reads 3,126 edited prompts (plan stage, 27B tokenizer); parts and readwrite ~1.5k and ~1.3k reads on forced cells; plus three 27B loads (~3 min each from local disk). At an assumed ~22 reads/s on the A100 PCIe (1/3 of the H200 throughput in EXPERIMENTS.md: map_A8_v1 64 reads/s) about 15 min. The ledger's run time calibrates the main jobs' estimates.

command: uv run python scripts/early_push.py run --name d4_push_v1 --why "D4: is a hard early lens push (layers 16-28, 4-16x the copy's norm) the same as editing the input word, or a write of the intermediate? Decides whether layers_v1's early RL flips contradict C2" --n 60
examples_command: uv run python scripts/early_push.py examples --name d4_push_v1
question: On Qwen3.6-27B at layers 16-28, does the lens push v_X - v_I that flips RL 35-61% and BL 24-44% act like putting X's word into the question (agreeing item by item with the text edits, not depending on the cue positions, moving BL as much as RL) or like writing the intermediate variable (agreeing with C's own in-transit state)?
why_it_matters: C2 says the lens cannot write a lookup-used bridge where the model carries it. layers_v1 found early pushes that flip RL (and BL, whose bridge the lens barely reads). H-inject keeps C2 (the early flips are input edits, upstream of where the bridge is carried); H-write kills C2 as stated (RL is writable, just early). It also tells the "around" route story whether early lens directions act on words or on variables.

hypotheses.H-inject: K1 dk = kappa(P*, E-insert) - kappa(P*, W-copy*) > 0 with CI above 0 (e.g. +0.2 to +0.4); flips(nb) >= flips(a)/2 (pushing everything but the subject phrase keeps >= half the effect; layers_v1's r-push, a subset of nb for RL, already flips RL 35-61%); BL within 15 points of RL at P* (e.g. 40% vs 50%); K4 cos(P*_b, E-name) - cos(P*_b, E-cue) > 0 at the final positions (layers 32-40); E-unrelated flips < 10%
hypotheses.H-write: dk < 0 with CI below 0; flips(b) >> flips(nb) and flips(nb) < flips(a)/2; BL < RL - 15 points (BL's bridge is not lens-readable at the question, so a lens write lands less); K4 < 0; P*_b's transit projection on C's copy delta at 44-52 >= E-name's

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/early_push.py's docstring and manifest before the run. P* = the lens push at subset a (whole question region + template) whose RL flip rate is nearest 50% over layers 16/20/24/28/band x scales 4/8/16; W-copy* per family = C's copy at 32-48 nearest 50%; emb* = the embedding push nearest 50% on RL. K1 (RL): CI of dk above 0 inject-like, below 0 write-like; counts only if the gate passes (kappa(emb*, E-insert) - kappa(emb*, W-copy*) CI above 0 on RL). K2 (RL, P*'s layer and scale): inject-like if flips(nb) - flips(a)/2 has CI above 0; write-like if that CI is below 0 and flips(b) - flips(nb) has CI above 0. K3: flips(BL) - flips(RL) at P*, paired by scene: inject-like if CI lower bound > -0.15, write-like if upper bound < -0.15. Verdict: "push behaves like an input-word edit" if >= 2 of K1-K3 inject-like and none write-like; "push writes the intermediate" if >= 2 write-like and none inject-like; otherwise mixed. K4/K5, countries, BR/RR, O, text loss reported, not decisive. Item bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 0.
controls: random direction at the same per-position norm for every lens push and embedding push (rules out any big push)
r-subset push = layers_v1's push on the same items (replication anchor; summary.json replication)
C's copy at r at 16-28 (the 0% anchor) and at 32-48 (W-copy*: the model's own in-transit variable, graded)
edited-input activation patch (Biran et al. 2024 back-patching): the C run's residual at a, at 16-28, raw and at the push's per-token norm
embedding push e_X - e_I and e_X at the subject phrase: the "edit the input word" limit; its kappa pattern is the gate for K1
E-unrelated: X named in an unrelated context sentence (does merely mentioning X move the answer?)
O (off-path prompt) under the push and WikiText next-token loss under the push vs random: collateral damage
countries R/B (bridge read and written by the lens at 44-52): the same measures where a lens write is known to work
n: 60 per family (BL, BR, RL, RR on the same 60 scenes, the first 60 of map_A8_v1 = a subset of layers_v1's 80; countries R, B 60 each)
notes: Timing: ~200 edited reads per item (150 lens/random pushes, 16 patches, 9 copies, 8 embedding pushes, 15 O pushes, 4 text edits) x 360 items = ~72k reads; at ~22 reads/s (A100 assumption shared by the D-jobs: 1/3 of the H200's 64/s; layers_v1 itself did 49,920 reads in 571 s = 87/s on the sprint box) ~55 min, + 27B load ~3 min, + per-item state metrics and Python overhead ~2 s/item ~12 min, + plain-text loss (4 pairs, 16 rows, 121 conditions, full sequences) ~3 min: ~1.2 h. Outputs are appended scene by scene (suite scenes first, countries last), so a stopped run keeps every finished scene. If tonight's budget is tight, --n 50 saves ~10 min. Layers 16 and 20 fall before the first third of depth (21.3 of 64: the paper's pre-workspace band), 24 and 28 after it. Results: results/early_push/d4_push_v1/.

command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py map --name d1_map_v1 --why "D1: where the lookup reads the bridge, statement positions vs question tokens (position-set x layer copy map)" --n 32 --layers 0 8 16 24 28 32 34 36 38 40 44 48 52 60
examples_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py examples --name d1_map_v1
question: Where, by position set (the bridge's binding statement, its word, the other bindings, the lookup rows, the whole context, the question, its words, the template tail) and layer, does each family carry its bridge, i.e. where does copying C's residual into the clean run give X's answer?
why_it_matters: Every "around" measure (copy split, lens read/write) was taken at the question tokens only. For bound bridges the bridge is stated in the context and only referred to in the question (lens reads BL there 7%; question copy moves BL only 10-17% at 32-40). If BL's bridge is still in transit at the statement positions at layers 32-40, the "around" result for lookups (claim C2: memory through the J-space, prompt lookups around it) may be a location artefact; d1_parts_v1 / d1_rw_v1 then test the J-space there. If BL has left the statements by 32, H-loc's location premise fails at the question-token layers.

hypotheses.H-loc: BL (and BLR): a statement set (bind_bridge, bridge_word, lookup_x or context) is in transit (C copy flips >= 50%, above controls) at >= 1 of layers 32-40, while the question set flips <= 20% there (map_A8_v1: 5-10%)
hypotheses.H-early-handoff: BL's statement sets stop being in transit before layer 32 (last transit layer <= 28) and no set flips >= 50% at 32-40 except context (the bridge is spread over the lookup rows / question words)
hypotheses.prior: Prior (Dan's agent, before any run): H-loc 0.55 (the question copy only takes over BL at 48-52, so the bridge must sit somewhere upstream at 32-40), H-early-handoff 0.45. Sanity expectations: every B family's bridge_word copy flips >= 90% at layer 0; RL/RR/R statement copies exact no-ops; countries B question set in transit by layer 40 (control_split map_v1: 81% at 40).

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (module docstring of scripts/statement_positions.py). Transit cell: C's copy gives X's answer in >= 50% of cases and its Wilson 95% lower bound exceeds the upper bound of every control's change rate (O's copy where non-zero; the random-direction copy at the same per-position norms); zero-delta cases count as unchanged. Handoff per family and statement set = the last transit layer. H-loc's location premise holds for BL if any statement set is in transit at a layer in [32, 44); it fails if none is. Run invalid if: identity changes the top token in any case, all0 misses C's top token in > 2% of cases, any causality violation (a predicted-zero cell with a non-zero delta), or read-vs-greedy agreement < 99%.
controls: O (off-path counterfactual: X's and Z's lockers / friends / rows / holders swapped) copied at the same cell, where its delta is non-zero: rules out "any change to these positions moves the answer"
random direction per position at the C copy's norm (same cell): rules out a norm / disruption effect, and is the only control at the binding statements (O is exactly zero there)
cue-only families (RL, RR, countries R): C's statement copies are exact no-ops by construction (verified numerically on every case and layer; read on the first 5 cases)
identity copy and C-at-every-position-at-layer-0 per case (hook checks); read vs greedy on the first 10 cases per family
paired readers: BL/BR (BLR/BRL) share scenes, so their statement-position patches are identical
n: 32 per family (BL, BR, RL, RR, BLR, BRL from suite_split map_A8_v1's case list; countries R, B from control_split map_v1's), i.e. read_write's case selection (first n per family)
notes: Time: 67,996 edited reads (plan stage on the 27B tokenizer: 14 layers x 9 sets x C / O / random, zero cells skipped). Throughput on the A100 PCIe assumed 22 reads/s = the H200 runs in EXPERIMENTS.md (map_A8_v1 76,800 reads in 1,205 s = 64/s; read_write layers_v1 87/s) divided by ~3 (bf16 312 vs 989 TFLOPs, 1.9 vs 4.8 TB/s) -> 0.86 h + 3 recording forwards per case + load ~ 0.95 h; d1_smoke_27b's ledger time recalibrates it. Layers: every 8th outside the handoff window, every 2nd in 28-40 (the question-token measures sit at 32-40; the question copy takes over BL at 44-52), the coarse grid's 32/36/40 for the parts / readwrite cells. n=32 sized to the night's 2.5 h D1 budget (Wilson half-width ~0.17 at 50%); a full run (n=80, every layer 32-52) is 4.2 h.

command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py parts --name d1_parts_v1 --map d1_map_v1 --why "D1: at the transit cells (statement positions vs question), is the copy's effect carried by its J-space part?" --lo 32 --sets bind_bridge bridge_word lookup_x context question
examples_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py examples --name d1_parts_v1
question: Where the bridge is in transit at layers 32-40 (d1_map_v1's transit cells), does the J-space part of C's copy carry more of its effect than its share of the copy predicts, at the statement positions as at the question tokens?
why_it_matters: Kills or supports the location-artefact reading of claim C2's "prompt lookups go around the J-space". At the statements BL and BR receive the identical patch (the context precedes the question), so a BL-BR concentration difference there isolates what the lookup reads from the same representation.

hypotheses.H-loc: at a BL (or BLR) statement set in transit at 32-40: J-space concentration lower bound > 1.2 and above the random-dictionary null's upper bound (countries at the question tokens: 2.5-2.9); BR minus BL concentration at the same cells within +-0.3
hypotheses.H-around: at every BL statement set in transit at 32-40: concentration upper bound < 1.0 (as at the question tokens: 0.3-0.4) with not_jspace - jspace > 0; BR (and countries B) at the same sets > 1.2; BR minus BL > 0.5
hypotheses.prior: Prior (Dan's agent): H-around 0.5, H-loc 0.25, inconclusive / empty cells 0.25. Reasons: the J-space part of the question-token copy never flipped any suite family; the bridge word at its own statement is a token the lens reads easily, which could favour H-loc at bridge_word only.

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (module docstring). Per family, set, primary window (layers 32/36/40 among the transit cells): inside if the J-space concentration (case bootstrap 95%) lower bound > 1.2 and above rand_omp's upper bound; around if the upper bound < 1.0 and not_jspace - jspace > 0 (paired bootstrap lower bound); else inconclusive (suite_split's 2.0 rule reported as verdict_strict). J-space half of D1: H-loc if any BL/BLR statement set is inside; H-around if all are around and the positive control (countries B, else BR) is inside at the same set; around without a passing positive control is not interpretable; no BL statement cell in transit at 32-40 = H-loc's location premise fails (reported, nothing to split).
controls: each part along a random direction at the same per-position norms (its null)
rand_omp: the same 25-atom OMP over a random dictionary (the fitting null for concentration)
jspace_matched / lens2_matched: equal-sized, equally aligned pieces of the copy
jspace_wo_own: the J-space part after the bridge's and X's own lens vectors are projected out (is it the word?)
O's full copy at the same cell; positive control: countries B (recall-used, lens-writable) at the same sets
n: up to 32 per family (d1_map_v1's cases), only families with transit cells
notes: Cells depend on the map. Time per cell ~1.1 s on the A100 (16 reads at ~22/s plus three 25-atom OMPs over ~200k letter-token vectors, fp32); expected ~4 cells per bound-family case and ~1 per cue-only case (~800 cells, 0.3 h); worst case (5 sets x 3 layers in every case) 1.2 h. One layer's dictionaries (two [letters, 5120] fp32 maps, ~8 GB) at a time next to the 27B (layer-major loop).

command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py readwrite --name d1_rw_v1 --map d1_map_v1 --parts d1_parts_v1 --why "D1: at the transit cells, does the J-lens read the bridge and does its direction write it?" --lo 32 --sets bind_bridge bridge_word lookup_x context question
examples_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py examples --name d1_rw_v1
question: At the cells where the bridge is in transit at layers 32-40, does the J-lens read it, and does pushing v_X - v_I (0.5-16x the copy's per-position norm) write X, as it does for countries at the question tokens?
why_it_matters: The lens-write half of D1's decision. "Read without write" (RL read 95%, written <= 3% at 32-40) is the strongest "around" evidence; if the lookup-used bound bridge is written by the lens where it is stated, the around result is a location artefact (H-loc); if it resists there too, "around" holds wherever the bridge is in transit (H-around).

hypotheses.H-loc: BL/BLR at a statement set in transit: lens flips >= 30% at <= 4x with random <= 5% (countries at the question tokens: 95-98% at 2-8x)
hypotheses.H-around: BL/BLR: lens - random flip difference upper bound < 10 points at every scale 0.5-16x at every statement set in transit; countries B / BR written at the same sets
hypotheses.note_on_read: At bridge_word the word is literally there: the lens read is expected high under both hypotheses (not discriminating); X's read at bind_bridge is the floor

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (module docstring). Per family, set, primary window: written if at some scale <= 4x lens flips >= 30% and the paired-bootstrap lower bound of lens - random flips > 0; not written if at every scale the difference's upper bound < 0.10; else inconclusive. Combined D1 verdict (summary "claims", with d1_parts_v1): H-loc supported for BL/BLR if a statement set in transit is J-space inside AND written; H-around supported if every statement set in transit is around AND not written AND the positive control is inside; else neither (mixed).
controls: a random direction per position at the same norms at every scale (rules out a pure norm effect)
C's copy at the same cell (the effect to explain)
X's rank at the same positions (the read's floor)
countries B and BR at the same sets (positive control: written at the question tokens)
n: up to 32 per family (d1_map_v1's cases), only families with transit cells
notes: Time: 13 reads per cell plus two recording forwards per case; expected ~800 cells -> ~10k reads at ~22/s ~ 0.15 h + load; worst case (15 cells in every case) 0.5 h.

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --name d3_main_27b --set main --n 25 --layers 16 18 20 22 24 26 28 30 32 34 36 38 40 42 44 46 48 50 52 54 56 58 60 --competence d3_competence_27b --why "D3 main: the three-way dissociation patch (identity / position / value) on main items, every 2nd layer 16-60" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_main_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3_main_27b
question: On held-out main items (N=5, four domains, RL/DL/RR on the same scenes), what does patching the dissoc source's residual (question / final / last / both; every 2nd layer 16-60 and the early, mid and transit windows) carry into the base - the bridge's identity, a pointer to its statement's position, or the answer value?
why_it_matters: The headline D3 test of the "around" route (C2). position at 44-52 => read-without-write is explained by a pointer the lens cannot express (H-pointer, the longshot); identity => a non-lens identity code (fit it, D3 fit stage); value => the lookup is finished before 44, so the "around" result at 44-52 is about timing and the write test belongs earlier (the 27B's 16-28 pushes, D4); none => the bridge is carried elsewhere (statements, D1).

hypotheses.H-pointer: RL final/last transit (44-52): position >= 50% [Wilson lower bound > identity and value upper bounds], RR position <= 10%, DL position >= 50%; by slot: position strongest for first/last, weaker in the middle
hypotheses.H-word: RL final/last transit: identity >= 50%, position <= 20%, value <= 20%
hypotheses.H-value: RL final/last transit: value >= 50%; last group value earlier (lower layer) than final
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: value 0.4, position 0.3, identity 0.3 (to be updated by the pilot before enqueuing).

decision_rule: As d3_pilot_27b (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring), applied to main items: primary cell RL x final x transit window (44-52) x dissoc, pooled over domains; supported hypothesis = the verdict (position -> H-pointer, identity -> H-word, value -> H-value; none/damage/mixed -> inconclusive). Secondary, reported not decisive: the same rule for group last and both, per layer, per domain, per queried slot (first/middle/last), DL and RR. A verdict that holds in fewer than 3 of 4 domains is reported as domain-dependent.
controls: same source (no-op under every hypothesis): damage
rand (matched-norm random direction): chance bar
other (another domain's item at matched norm): realistic null / domain-general positional code
context digits predicted by no hypothesis: per-digit chance inside the runs
self no-op and layer-0 all-position reproduction: hook checks (run invalid if either < 100% top agreement)
n: 25 scenes per domain x 4 domains = 100 per family (300 cases); Wilson half-width ~10 points at 50%
notes: Reads per case: 3 + 23 layers x 4 groups x 2 + 12 x 4 x 2 + 3 windows x 4 x 2 = 307 -> 92k reads; at ~22/s (A100 estimate, see d3_pilot_27b) ~70 min + load -> 1.2 h. Enqueue only after a human has read the pilot (the queue would run it as soon as the pilot is done). If the pilot shows the action is all above 44, drop layers 16-30 and raise n to 40 per domain at the same cost.

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --name d3_pilot_levels_27b --set dev --levels e3f0 e5f4 --n 15 --layer-step 4 --competence d3_competence_27b --why "D3 levels: does the identity/position/value split change with 3 statements, or with filler sentences between the statements?" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_pilot_levels_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3_pilot_levels_27b
question: Same patch as d3_pilot_27b (dev items, every 4th layer, question / final / last / question+final, plus the early/mid/transit windows), on the two other dev levels: N=3 statements (e3f0) and N=5 statements with 4 filler sentences woven in (e5f4; the filler layout is the same in base and source). Does the RL split between identity, position and value change against the pilot's e5f0?
why_it_matters: Tests whether the pilot's outcome is specific to 5 adjacent statements. Mixing Mechanisms (Gur-Arieh et al. 2025) predicts the positional route dominates more with fewer entities (N=3). Filler between the statements moves them to other token positions and breaks their adjacency: a pointer that survives it indexes statements, not a fixed neighbourhood. Limitation: the filler layout is shared by base and source, so this does not separate statement order from absolute token offset (that needs an offset-shift variant, not built).

hypotheses.H-robust: RL final/last at the transit window: the pilot's winning outcome keeps its share at e5f4 within 0.15
hypotheses.H-contiguity: the winning outcome's share drops by more than 0.15 with filler (e5f4 vs e5f0)
hypotheses.H-fewer-entities: position share at e3f0 above e5f0 by more than 0.15 (positional route dominates at N=3)
hypotheses.prior: Coordinator prior: H-robust 0.65; H-fewer-entities 0.4.

decision_rule: Per level, the pilot's rule (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring) on the primary cell (RL, final, transit, pooled over domains). Level effects: difference in each outcome's share against d3_pilot_27b's e5f0 cell with a 95% Newcombe interval; 'same' if the interval lies within +-0.15, 'differs' if it excludes 0 and exceeds 0.15 in magnitude, else 'unclear'. Interpreted only if both levels pass the interpretability condition (patch changes the answer >= 20% lower bound, 'same' control <= 10% upper bound).
controls: same source (q_s = q_b at the same slot, same digit, rest of the context reshuffled and redigited): every hypothesis predicts the base answer; rules out damage from patching a residual computed on another context
rand: seeded random direction at the dissoc patch's per-position norm: rules out generic disruption picking a context digit (chance bar for identity/position)
other: another domain's item (same family), its residual at the same distance from the prompt end, rescaled to the dissoc norm: realistic-activation null; also probes a domain-general positional code
context digits predicted by no hypothesis (N=5: 2 per item): the per-digit chance rate inside the same runs
base into base at the middle layer (no-op) and layer-0 all-position patch (reproduces the source): hook checks
n: 15 scenes per domain x 4 domains = 60 per family per level (e3f0, e5f4), dev items
notes: Two levels x d3_pilot_27b's per-level cost (0.55 h est): 1.1 h est; d3_smoke_27b measured 31 edited reads/s on this A100 (1476 reads in 48 s), so likely ~0.8 h. Dev items are never headline items.

command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py map --name d1_map_n80_v1 --why "D1 confirmatory map: n=80 per family at the layers where H-loc is decided (32-52)" --n 80 --layers 32 34 36 38 40 44 48 52
examples_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py examples --name d1_map_n80_v1
question: Same as d1_map_v1, at n=80 per family and only layers 32-52 (where H-loc vs H-early-handoff is decided).
why_it_matters: Every "around" measure (copy split, lens read/write) was taken at the question tokens only. For bound bridges the bridge is stated in the context and only referred to in the question (lens reads BL there 7%; question copy moves BL only 10-17% at 32-40). If BL's bridge is still in transit at the statement positions at layers 32-40, the "around" result for lookups (claim C2: memory through the J-space, prompt lookups around it) may be a location artefact; d1_parts_v1 / d1_rw_v1 then test the J-space there. If BL has left the statements by 32, H-loc's location premise fails at the question-token layers. This run is the confirmatory version of d1_map_v1's transit verdicts: n=80 gives Wilson half-widths of about +-0.11 at 50% instead of +-0.17 at n=32, on the same rule.

hypotheses.H-loc: BL (and BLR): a statement set (bind_bridge, bridge_word, lookup_x or context) is in transit (C copy flips >= 50%, above controls) at >= 1 of layers 32-40, while the question set flips <= 20% there (map_A8_v1: 5-10%)
hypotheses.H-early-handoff: BL's statement sets stop being in transit before layer 32 (last transit layer <= 28) and no set flips >= 50% at 32-40 except context (the bridge is spread over the lookup rows / question words)
hypotheses.prior: Prior (Dan's agent, before any run): H-loc 0.55 (the question copy only takes over BL at 48-52, so the bridge must sit somewhere upstream at 32-40), H-early-handoff 0.45. Sanity expectations: every B family's bridge_word copy flips >= 90% at layer 0; RL/RR/R statement copies exact no-ops; countries B question set in transit by layer 40 (control_split map_v1: 81% at 40).

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (module docstring of scripts/statement_positions.py). Transit cell: C's copy gives X's answer in >= 50% of cases and its Wilson 95% lower bound exceeds the upper bound of every control's change rate (O's copy where non-zero; the random-direction copy at the same per-position norms); zero-delta cases count as unchanged. Handoff per family and statement set = the last transit layer. H-loc's location premise holds for BL if any statement set is in transit at a layer in [32, 44); it fails if none is. Run invalid if: identity changes the top token in any case, all0 misses C's top token in > 2% of cases, any causality violation (a predicted-zero cell with a non-zero delta), or read-vs-greedy agreement < 99%.
controls: O (off-path counterfactual: X's and Z's lockers / friends / rows / holders swapped) copied at the same cell, where its delta is non-zero: rules out "any change to these positions moves the answer"
random direction per position at the C copy's norm (same cell): rules out a norm / disruption effect, and is the only control at the binding statements (O is exactly zero there)
cue-only families (RL, RR, countries R): C's statement copies are exact no-ops by construction (verified numerically on every case and layer; read on the first 5 cases)
identity copy and C-at-every-position-at-layer-0 per case (hook checks); read vs greedy on the first 10 cases per family
paired readers: BL/BR (BLR/BRL) share scenes, so their statement-position patches are identical
n: 80 per family (BL, BR, RL, RR, BLR, BRL, countries R, B), layers 32 34 36 38 40 44 48 52
notes: Not a replacement: d1_parts_v1 / d1_rw_v1 use d1_map_v1's cells. Reads: d1_map_v1's 67,996 x (8/14 layers) x (80/32 cases) ~ 97k; at the measured 31 reads/s ~ 0.9 h + load; est 1.2 h. Rules and hypotheses copied from d1_map_v1 unchanged.

command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_smoke_27b --why "D2 27B smoke: every condition type of the attention/DeltaNet edge knock-out, n=4 per family, before the main runs" --n 4 --layers all win8k pre suf kind --sweep path+random --sweep-dests both --absent && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_smoke_27b && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_smoke_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name d2_smoke_27b --k 2
question: Does the exact edge knock-out (bridge_jspace.knockout) run on Qwen3.6-27B for every condition type, with an exact no-op, a passing positive control, and a throughput that fits tonight's D2 budget?
why_it_matters: Gate for d2_ko_core_v1, d2_ko_sweep_v1 and d2_ko_tie_country_v1. The knock-out is new code (masked full-attention logits; a second Gated DeltaNet run with the source's values zeroed); tested exactly against fp64 references on a tiny model and on Qwen3.5-0.8B (fp32, CPU and fla), but never on the 27B's bf16 forward.

hypotheses.H-noop: check.json noop_empty_source_max_abs == 0 (an empty source span leaves the answer read bit-for-bit unchanged; 0.8B smoke: 0.0)
hypotheses.H-posctl: check.json posctl_last_reads_nothing_max_abs and posctl_context_erased_absent_max_abs < 0.1 logits with the same top token (0.8B smoke: 0.0 and 0.0, vs 2.4 unhooked)
hypotheses.H-throughput: timing.json rows_per_second >= 15 (assumed 20; 0.8B smoke 106 rows/s, overhead of a batch knocked at every layer 1.8x on the 0.8B, expected <= 1.3x on the 27B where the DeltaNet mixer is ~27% of a layer)

decision_rule: The main D2 jobs are interpreted only if this job exits 0 with check.json passed = true (no-op exact, positive controls within 0.1 logits, same top token). If rows_per_second < 15, the human shrinks n of the main jobs before they start (their est_gpu_hours assume 20). No scientific claim from this run (n=4).
controls: no-op: an empty source span at every layer (must be bit-exact)

positive control 1: every token but the first and the last blocked from the last at every layer, DeltaNet mode absent, on the prompt and on the same prompt with its context tokens rolled: the last logits must not differ
positive control 2: the whole context blocked from every later position at every layer (mode absent): same
kernel path: one DeltaNet layer's real inputs through fla and through transformers' torch reference, with and without the values zeroed at the source (recorded, not gated)
unedited row in every batch (the baseline of its batch's knocked rows; its drift from a plain forward recorded)
n: 4 per family (BL, BR, RL, RR, BLR, BRL from suite_split map_A8_v1's case list; countries R, B from control_split map_v1's)
notes: Rows: 5,838 knocked reads (rows per item counted with the script's own conditions() on a 64-layer hybrid: BL/BLR/BRL 236, BR/RL/RR 156, countries ~142). At an assumed 20 rows/s on the A100 PCIe (D1's 22 reads/s from the H200 runs in EXPERIMENTS.md divided by ~3, minus ~8% knock-out overhead): ~5 min, plus load and the check stage ~4-5 min.

command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_ko_core_v1 --why "D2 core contrast: block question/final positions from the lookup or binding statement (vs off-path, random, trailing spans) at all layers and in 8-layer windows split by attention / DeltaNet; does RL break while RR survives?" --families BL BR RL RR --n 60 --layers all win8k kind --sweep path+random --absent && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_ko_core_v1 && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_ko_core_v1
examples_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name d2_ko_core_v1 --k 3
question: When the question tokens and/or the final template positions cannot read the lookup statement ("The cow's locker is 5.") directly, does RL (recalled bridge -> in-prompt lookup) break while RR (same scenes, recall from memory) survives; which destinations must see it, and in which 8-layer window, through attention or DeltaNet layers?
why_it_matters: C1 (prompt lookups go around the J-space). The lens reads RL's bridge at 32-40 but cannot write it, and copying C's question-group residual flips RL 98-100% only at 44-52 (EXPERIMENTS rows 27, 52). If the answer site reads the statement directly and late (H_answer_site), the lookup needs no J-space-written bridge at the question tokens: a concrete "around" route (a pointer/lookback-style read). If instead the question tokens read the statement and relay it (H_relay), the around route runs through the question tokens, where the copy split measured it. RR/BR give the matched contrast: same scenes and statement, no lookup.

hypotheses.H_answer_site: BL and RL: (lookup, final, all) accuracy <= 40% (NEEDED) and (lookup, question, all) >= 90% (not NEEDED); RR and BR: every lookup cell (question / final / both / after, mode value) >= 95%; the lookup->final window effect sits at or after layer 40: no window below 32 NEEDED, win40-47 or win48-55 NEEDED or PARTIAL. Prior 0.5
hypotheses.H_relay: BL and RL: (lookup, question, all) NEEDED and (lookup, final, all) not NEEDED. Prior 0.2
hypotheses.H_both_routes: neither question nor final alone is NEEDED but both is (redundant routes). Prior 0.3
hypotheses.H_binding: BL and BR: (binding, question, all) NEEDED; BR: (binding, final, all) >= 90%. Pointer variant (H_ptr, prior 0.35): BL also needs (binding, final, all) (NEEDED or PARTIAL) while BR does not
hypotheses.H_kind: no prior direction: the attention-only and DeltaNet-only halves of the needed windows are reported; the answer-site read is predicted to need the 2 attention layers of its window (>= 2/3 of the window's accuracy drop) with prior 0.5
hypotheses.positive_control: every path source at (after, all, mode absent): accuracy <= 30% (lockers: one of 3 in the prompt; BR binding: legs guessable ~45%, so <= 60% there)

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/attn_knockout.py docstring, manifest "decision"). Items: unedited read right. A cell (family, source, destination, layer set, DeltaNet mode) is NEEDED if accuracy drops >= 20 points and the paired bootstrap 95% lower bound of acc(matched control) - acc(cell) is >= 10 points (lookup_off for lookup, binding_off for binding; same destination, layers, mode); NOT NEEDED if the Wilson 95% lower bound of accuracy is >= 90%; otherwise PARTIAL. A family whose path sources fail the positive control is not interpreted. C1a ("RL breaks, RR survives") holds if RL (lookup, both, all) is NEEDED and RR (lookup, both, all) NOT NEEDED. C1b (answer site) / relay as H_answer_site / H_relay above, on BL and RL. Control damage (random, trailing, *_off cells with a >= 20 point drop) is reported next to every NEEDED cell.
controls: lookup_off / binding_off: another statement of the same kind and token length (seeded per scene): rules out "any statement-sized hole at these positions breaks the answer"
random: a seeded contiguous context span of the lookup's length, overlapping no path statement
trailing: the up-to-3 context tokens right after the lookup statement (the DeltaNet conv's reach): what blocking them alone does
RR and BR: the same scenes and statements, answer recalled: rules out damage to the final positions in general
positive control: path sources invisible to every later position at every layer, DeltaNet mode absent
unedited row in every batch (baseline of that batch); check.json no-op / positive control gate before the run
n: 60 scenes per family (BL, BR, RL, RR on the same scenes; the first 60 of suite_split map_A8_v1's seed-0 sample)
notes: Rows: 74,160 knocked reads (per item: BL 426, BR/RL/RR 270; 36 all-layer cells incl. mode absent, plus 24 window sets (8 windows x both / attention-only / DeltaNet-only) + 2 kind sets x 3 destinations x the sweep sources). At an assumed 20 rows/s on the A100 PCIe: 62 min + load/check ~5 min. d2_smoke_27b's timing.json recalibrates it. n=60: Wilson half-width ~10 points at 80%.

command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_ko_sweep_v1 --why "D2 fine layer sweep: stride-4 8-layer windows and prefix/suffix cuts every 8 layers, path statements and their same-kind controls, BL/BR/RL/RR" --families BL BR RL RR --n 30 --layers all win4 pre suf --sweep path --absent && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_ko_sweep_v1 && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_ko_sweep_v1
examples_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name d2_ko_sweep_v1 --k 3
question: Over which layers must the lookup statement stay readable from the final positions (and the binding statement from the question tokens) for BL and RL to keep their answer, compared with the copy's transit band (44-52) and the lens's write failure (32-52)?
why_it_matters: Localises the C1 read in depth with redundancy handled: suffix cuts [L, 64) give the last layer the read can still happen at (suf_max_needed); prefix cuts [0, L) the first layer by which it must have happened (pre_min_needed). A late band overlapping 44-52 puts the lookup's read where the bridge is in transit and the lens cannot write: the around route acts there. An early band (< 32) would mean the statement is read before the J-space layers we measured.

hypotheses.H_late_band: RL and BL lookup->final: suf_max_needed >= 40 and pre_min_needed >= 48 (blocking [0, 40) does not matter, blocking [40, 64) does): the band lies in 40-56. Prior 0.5
hypotheses.H_early_band: RL lookup->final or ->question: pre_min_needed <= 32 and suf_max_needed <= 32. Prior 0.25
hypotheses.H_spread: no single prefix or suffix cut below the full set is NEEDED (redundant reads across depth). Prior 0.25
hypotheses.H_binding_band: BL and BR binding->question: needed before layer 32 (pre_min_needed <= 32 or a stride-4 window below 32 NEEDED). BL vs BR the same band (prior 0.6); BL later than BR (the lookup dereferences a pointer late, prior 0.4)
hypotheses.RR_null: RR and BR: every lookup cell >= 95% at every layer set

decision_rule: As d2_ko_core_v1 (NEEDED / NOT NEEDED / PARTIAL per cell, matched controls lookup_off and binding_off at the same destination and layer set). Band per family x source x destination: suf_max_needed = the largest L with suf L NEEDED; pre_min_needed = the smallest L with pre L NEEDED; windows_needed listed. H_late_band holds for a family if suf_max_needed >= 40 and pre_min_needed >= 48 (or no pre cut below 64 is NEEDED while suf40 is).
controls: lookup_off / binding_off at the same destination and layer set (same kind, same token length)
RR (same scenes, recall) under the same lookup cuts: rules out generic damage from cutting the final positions off a statement over a band of layers
positive control and check gate as d2_ko_core_v1
n: 30 scenes per family (the first 30 of suite_split map_A8_v1's seed-0 sample, a subset of d2_ko_core_v1's)
notes: Rows: 30,420 knocked reads (per item: BL 384, BR/RL/RR 210; 29 layer sets = 15 stride-4 windows + 7 prefix + 7 suffix cuts, x 3 destinations x path sources and their controls; plus the all-layer cells). At an assumed 20 rows/s: 25 min + load/check ~5 min. n=30 is a localisation profile (Wilson half-width ~15 points at 70%), not a headline; a NEEDED band is then confirmed at n >= 100 in a follow-up.

command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_ko_tie_country_v1 --why "D2 on the tie-breakers (BLR lookup->recall, BRL recall->lookup) and countries R/B: which statements must be visible from which positions, at which layers" --families BLR BRL country-R country-B --n 25 --layers all win8k pre suf --sweep path --absent && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_ko_tie_country_v1 && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_ko_tie_country_v1
examples_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name d2_ko_tie_country_v1 --k 3
question: In the three-step families, where the use of the bridge and the source of the answer come apart, and in the paper-style countries (B bound, R recalled), which statements must the question and final positions read directly, and when?
why_it_matters: Separates "what uses the bridge" from "where the answer comes from" for the direct-read route. BLR (bound -> lookup -> recall): if its lookup must also be read at the answer site, the recall that follows has to run in the last layers; if it is read earlier (from the question tokens), the lookup feeds a recall like a recalled bridge (C1 vs C2 boundary). BRL (bound -> recall -> lookup) should need its row statement late at the final positions like BL. Countries B is the J-space-inside case (copy split 2.5, lens writes it): its binding statement should be read into the question tokens, not at the answer site.

hypotheses.H_BLR_early: BLR (lookup, question, all) NEEDED and its lookup->final pre_min_needed <= 40 (read earlier than BL's, to leave depth for the recall). Prior 0.5
hypotheses.H_BRL_like_BL: BRL (lookup, final, all) NEEDED and (lookup, question, all) not NEEDED (the row read at the answer site). Prior 0.55
hypotheses.H_country_B: country-B (binding, question, all) NEEDED; (binding, final, all) >= 90%. Prior 0.6
hypotheses.H_country_R_null: country-R (binding: the statement only naming the bridge) >= 95% in every cell (the recall does not read it). Prior 0.8
hypotheses.positive_control: path sources at (after, all, mode absent) <= 30% (country-B <= 40%: capitals of 3 countries guessable from the prompt's countries)

decision_rule: As d2_ko_core_v1 (per-cell NEEDED / NOT NEEDED / PARTIAL against lookup_off / binding_off at the same destination, layers and mode; positive control per family). Bands as d2_ko_sweep_v1 (stride-8 windows here, each also split into its attention-only and DeltaNet-only layers).
controls: lookup_off / binding_off (same kind, same token length; for countries another "X lives in Y." of the same length where one exists, else flagged length_mismatch in cases.jsonl)
random and trailing spans (all layers)
country-R vs country-B: same statement form, used only by B
positive control and check gate as d2_ko_core_v1
n: 25 per family (BLR, BRL on the same scenes, suite_split map_A8_v1's first 25 tie scenes; countries, control_split map_v1's first 25 per family)
notes: Rows: ~37,100 knocked reads (per item: BLR/BRL ~492, countries ~250; counted with conditions() on a 64-layer hybrid). At an assumed 20 rows/s: 31 min + load/check ~5 min. Lowest priority of the D2 jobs: queue last.

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --name d3_main_ae_27b --set main --n 50 --domains animals elements --layers 16 18 20 22 24 26 28 30 32 34 36 38 40 42 44 46 48 50 52 54 56 58 60 --competence d3_competence_27b --why "D3 main on the domains that pass the competence gate (animals, elements): the three-way dissociation patch, every 2nd layer 16-60" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_main_ae_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3_main_ae_27b
question: On held-out main items (N=5, four domains, RL/DL/RR on the same scenes), what does patching the dissoc source's residual (question / final / last / both; every 2nd layer 16-60 and the early, mid and transit windows) carry into the base - the bridge's identity, a pointer to its statement's position, or the answer value?
why_it_matters: The headline D3 test of the "around" route (C2). position at 44-52 => read-without-write is explained by a pointer the lens cannot express (H-pointer, the longshot); identity => a non-lens identity code (fit it, D3 fit stage); value => the lookup is finished before 44, so the "around" result at 44-52 is about timing and the write test belongs earlier (the 27B's 16-28 pushes, D4); none => the bridge is carried elsewhere (statements, D1).

hypotheses.H-pointer: RL final/last transit (44-52): position >= 50% [Wilson lower bound > identity and value upper bounds], RR position <= 10%, DL position >= 50%; by slot: position strongest for first/last, weaker in the middle
hypotheses.H-word: RL final/last transit: identity >= 50%, position <= 20%, value <= 20%
hypotheses.H-value: RL final/last transit: value >= 50%; last group value earlier (lower layer) than final
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: value 0.4, position 0.3, identity 0.3 (to be updated by the pilot before enqueuing).

decision_rule: As d3_pilot_27b (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring), applied to main items: primary cell RL x final x transit window (44-52) x dissoc, pooled over domains; supported hypothesis = the verdict (position -> H-pointer, identity -> H-word, value -> H-value; none/damage/mixed -> inconclusive). Secondary, reported not decisive: the same rule for group last and both, per layer, per domain, per queried slot (first/middle/last), DL and RR. A verdict that holds in fewer than 3 of 4 domains is reported as domain-dependent.
controls: same source (no-op under every hypothesis): damage
rand (matched-norm random direction): chance bar
other (another domain's item at matched norm): realistic null / domain-general positional code
context digits predicted by no hypothesis: per-digit chance inside the runs
self no-op and layer-0 all-position reproduction: hook checks (run invalid if either < 100% top agreement)
n: 50 scenes per domain x 2 domains (animals, elements) = 100 per family (RL, DL, RR), main N=5
notes: d3_pilot_27b came out 'damage' in every cell, including layer 0 where nothing changes, because its n was 34 per family (months and planets gave 2 eligible scenes each) and the rule asks the 'same' control's Wilson upper bound to be <= 0.10, which needs n >= 35 even at 0 changes (3.84 / (n + 3.84)). This version applies the pre-registered competence gate (a domain x family cell enters iff its clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85, d3_competence_27b): months RL (46%), planets RR (55%) and planets RL (lower bound 0.84) fail, so only domains passing in all three families are used, and n is raised so the rule can pass. Controls, decision rule and hypotheses unchanged. Timing: d3_pilot_27b ran 102 cases x 16 layers in 601 s (37 reads/s); this run is 300 cases x 23 layers, about 45 min.

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --name d3_levels_animals_27b --set dev --levels e3f0 e5f0 e5f4 --domains animals --n 60 --layer-step 4 --competence d3_competence_27b --why "D3 levels on animals: does the split change with 3 statements, or with filler sentences between the statements?" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_levels_animals_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3_levels_animals_27b
question: Same patch as d3_pilot_27b (dev items, every 4th layer, question / final / last / question+final, plus the early/mid/transit windows), on the two other dev levels: N=3 statements (e3f0) and N=5 statements with 4 filler sentences woven in (e5f4; the filler layout is the same in base and source). Does the RL split between identity, position and value change against the pilot's e5f0?
why_it_matters: Tests whether the pilot's outcome is specific to 5 adjacent statements. Mixing Mechanisms (Gur-Arieh et al. 2025) predicts the positional route dominates more with fewer entities (N=3). Filler between the statements moves them to other token positions and breaks their adjacency: a pointer that survives it indexes statements, not a fixed neighbourhood. Limitation: the filler layout is shared by base and source, so this does not separate statement order from absolute token offset (that needs an offset-shift variant, not built).

hypotheses.H-robust: RL final/last at the transit window: the pilot's winning outcome keeps its share at e5f4 within 0.15
hypotheses.H-contiguity: the winning outcome's share drops by more than 0.15 with filler (e5f4 vs e5f0)
hypotheses.H-fewer-entities: position share at e3f0 above e5f0 by more than 0.15 (positional route dominates at N=3)
hypotheses.prior: Coordinator prior: H-robust 0.65; H-fewer-entities 0.4.

decision_rule: Per level, the pilot's rule (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring) on the primary cell (RL, final, transit, pooled over domains). Level effects: difference in each outcome's share against this run's own e5f0 cell with a 95% Newcombe interval; 'same' if the interval lies within +-0.15, 'differs' if it excludes 0 and exceeds 0.15 in magnitude, else 'unclear'. Interpreted only if both levels pass the interpretability condition (patch changes the answer >= 20% lower bound, 'same' control <= 10% upper bound).
controls: same source (q_s = q_b at the same slot, same digit, rest of the context reshuffled and redigited): every hypothesis predicts the base answer; rules out damage from patching a residual computed on another context
rand: seeded random direction at the dissoc patch's per-position norm: rules out generic disruption picking a context digit (chance bar for identity/position)
other: another domain's item (same family), its residual at the same distance from the prompt end, rescaled to the dissoc norm: realistic-activation null; also probes a domain-general positional code
context digits predicted by no hypothesis (N=5: 2 per item): the per-digit chance rate inside the same runs
base into base at the middle layer (no-op) and layer-0 all-position patch (reproduces the source): hook checks
n: 60 scenes per level (e3f0, e5f0, e5f4), animals only (the only domain passing the gate at every level), dev items
notes: d3_pilot_27b came out 'damage' in every cell, including layer 0 where nothing changes, because its n was 34 per family (months and planets gave 2 eligible scenes each) and the rule asks the 'same' control's Wilson upper bound to be <= 0.10, which needs n >= 35 even at 0 changes (3.84 / (n + 3.84)). This version applies the pre-registered competence gate (a domain x family cell enters iff its clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85, d3_competence_27b): months RL (46%), planets RR (55%) and planets RL (lower bound 0.84) fail, so only domains passing in all three families are used, and n is raised so the rule can pass. Controls, decision rule and hypotheses unchanged. Here elements also fail at e5f4 (RL lower bound 0.74), so animals only; e5f0 is rerun in the same job as the within-run baseline. Timing: 3 x 180 cases x 16 layers at 37 reads/s, about 35-40 min.

title: D3 alias gate: can the 27B look up statements written in French/Spanish/German or with the chemical symbol?
command: uv run python scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py manifest --set main dev --name alias_competence_27b --limit 200 --why "D3 alias gate: can the 27B look up a statement that names the entity in French/Spanish/German (animals) or by its chemical symbol (elements), on the same scenes as statements in English, every alt and control prompt and each step alone?" && uv run python scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py competence --name alias_competence_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py examples --name alias_competence_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py figures --name alias_competence_27b
question: On alias_pointer_v1 (pointer_v1's scenes; the statements in English, or naming the entity in French/Spanish/German for animals and by the chemical symbol for elements; the question always English), does Qwen3.6-27B answer the org prompt, the alt prompt, the two control prompts and each step alone (cue -> entity; the lookup with the entity named or the recalled fact; the other form -> English name) for memory → prompt, named → prompt and memory → memory?
why_it_matters: Gate for the alias patching run (pointer_swap on data/alias_pointer_v1). In pointer_v1 every statement repeats the word the model recalls ("cow"), so matching by that word and matching by meaning look the same. D3's first night (UNVERIFIED) found that after the question, at layers 44-50, memory → prompt carries the statement slot more often than the entity (29% vs 9%). If the 27B can look up statements that do not contain the recalled word, the same patch on this data asks whether that slot pointer (and the smaller entity share) survives when the statement is in another language or uses a symbol: answer of bridge alt's statement with French/Spanish/German statements => the lookup matches by meaning, not by the token the J-lens reads; answer at the same statement slot in every form => a positional pointer that ignores the surface form; entity share only with English statements => a lexical key. A failed gate for memory → prompt with named → prompt passing is itself a result: a recalled bridge cannot find a statement that does not repeat its word.

hypotheses.H-meaning: statements in French/Spanish/German: named → prompt >= 95% and memory → prompt >= 90% (org prompt), each within 5 points of statements in English on the same scenes; the other form -> English name step >= 95%
hypotheses.H-symbol: statements with the chemical symbol: named → prompt >= 90%, memory → prompt >= 85% (pointer_v1 elements, memory → prompt in English: 94% [88, 97])
hypotheses.H-lexical-crutch: memory → prompt with another form < 80% while named → prompt with it >= 90% and memory → prompt in English >= 95%
hypotheses.H-alias-unknown: the other form -> English name step < 90% for some entities (porc, pollo; He read as a pronoun, C or N as letters): those items drop out of the usable set; the gate can still pass
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior (written before any run): H-meaning 0.6 (the suite's translated-word family is answered by the 27B); H-symbol 0.5; H-lexical-crutch 0.25; H-alias-unknown 0.4. Statements in English: >= 95% in every animals cell; elements as pointer_v1 (memory → prompt 94%).

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py docstring, "Gate"). Per domain on main (first 200 scenes per file): the other form enters the patching run iff the org prompt's Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.80 in both memory → prompt and named → prompt, the statements-in-English cells of that domain pass pointer_v1's rule (lower bound >= 0.85), and >= 35 scenes are usable (every prompt of every family right) in both forms. Usable per item = every prompt right (org, alt, both controls, the steps alone). Report the answer read vs greedy agreement (must be >= 99%) and the paired-by-scene counts (both right / English only / other form only / neither). Dev cells (3 and 5 statements, 60 scenes) are a pilot, never the gate.
controls: statements in English on the same scenes (paired): separates the surface form from scene difficulty
each step alone (cue -> entity; the lookup with the entity named or the recalled fact; the other form -> English name): separates a composition failure from a missing translation or symbol
memory → memory on the same contexts: it does not need the statements, so a drop there is damage from a foreign context, not a lookup failure
answer read vs 8-token greedy: validates the one-forward read the patching runs use
n: gate cuts (domain x form x family, main): 200 scenes each (>= 35); usable-scene count per (domain, form): up to 200; dev cells: 60 each. 2400 main + 1440 dev items, 21760 prompts
notes: Greedy, no sampling seeds; item seeds are alias_pointer_v1's (main 711, dev 712). Time from the measured rate of d3_competence_27b (17920 prompts of the same shape: 545 s generate + 454 s read on this A100, 17.9 prompts/s): 21760 prompts ~ 1210 s + model load ~ 0.4 h; 0.45 h with margin. The 0.8B smoke (qwen35_08b_smoke_alias_comp2, 3 items per file, 612 prompts, 6 s) checks the code path only. Needs scripts/alias_pointer_v1.py and data/alias_pointer_v1/ committed before enqueueing.

title: D3 v2 test run: the new scenes and the --data option work on the 27B
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --data pointer_v2 --set main --name d3v2_smoke_27b --families RL DL --n 1 --layers 16 28 40 48 52 56 --groups question final last --question-max-layer 38 --control-levels e5-pln --no-eligibility --why "D3 v2 smoke: every stage on the 27B with pointer_v2's three types, hooks, no-op and positive controls, timing" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3v2_smoke_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3v2_smoke_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py figures --name d3v2_smoke_27b
question: Do pointer_swap's run / examples / figures stages work end to end on the 27B with --data pointer_v2 (three item types per scene, a token-position outcome, the reflexive contrast), with the self no-op and the layer-0 reproduction checks passing, and how many edited reads per second does it reach?
why_it_matters: Code-path and timing check before d3v2_offset_reflexive_main; no claim.

hypotheses.H-ok: self no-op and layer-0 reproduction 12/12; >= 30 edited reads/s
hypotheses.H-broken: any check below 12/12: the hooks or the token alignment are wrong; stop the queue

decision_rule: The main v2 run proceeds only if both checks are 12/12 (summary.json checks).
controls: org prompt patched into itself at the middle layer (must change nothing)
alt prompt patched at every position at layer 0 (must give the alt prompt's own answer)
n: 1 scene per topic x 2 families x 3 types = 12 cases
notes: The 0.8B smoke (same stages, layers 0-20) passed both checks; 27B rate on this A100: 31-38 reads/s.

title: D3b smoke: fitted slot direction, every stage on a few items
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py run --name d3b_slot_direction_smoke_27b --why "D3b 27B smoke: collect, fit, geometry and steer end to end on 40 fit items per domain and 4 + 4 held-out items per domain before the main run" --fit-limit 40 --n-test 4 --rr-n 4
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py examples --name d3b_slot_direction_smoke_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py figures --name d3b_slot_direction_smoke_27b
question: Does every pointer_fit stage (collect the states after the question, fit the slot directions and subspaces, geometry against the lens, steer with every condition, examples, figures) run on Qwen3.6-27B?
why_it_matters: Fail-fast gate for d3b_slot_direction_main_27b, the test of whether the "around" route is a statement pointer a fitted direction can steer. Not a result: n is tiny.

hypotheses.H-code-ok: fit.json has a decode_cv per collect layer and a geometry row per steer layer; unedited held-out items keep answer org on >= 15/16 (they passed the competence gate); the alt-prompt patch at layer 48 changes the answer on >= 1 of 8 memory → prompt items (D3 found 29% slot answers); outcomes.jsonl has 1 + 6 x (4 x 11 + 1) rows per memory → prompt item and 1 + 6 x (4 x 4 + 1) per memory → memory item; examples.json and one figures folder written
hypotheses.H-bug: any check fails or a stage crashes

decision_rule: Run d3b_slot_direction_main_27b only if every H-code-ok check holds; otherwise cancel it and read the log.
controls: unedited read of every held-out item (answer org expected: the competence gate)
alt-prompt patch (positive reference: D3's slot answers)
random push and shuffled-label direction at the same size (should not move the answer)
n: 40 fit items per domain; 4 memory → prompt and 4 memory → memory held-out items per domain
notes: Timing: ~2.9k edited reads at 31-37 reads/s (the A100 rate for the 27B) ~1.5 min, + one 27B load and the J++ lens ~4 min, + the geometry (letter-token dictionary and a random dictionary, ~5 GB each, at 5 layers) ~2 min: ~0.15 h. The 0.8B smoke (qwen35_08b_smoke_d3b_v1, layers 15-19) ran every stage in 43 s. Results: results/pointer_fit/d3b_slot_direction_smoke_27b/.

title: D3 v2 gate: can the 27B answer the new scenes (a filler sentence among the statements; alt answers also in the org prompt)?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_v2.py manifest --set main n3 --name d3v2_competence_27b --why "D3 v2 gate: can the 27B answer pointer_v2's scenes (5 or 3 statements plus one filler sentence of the same length; animals and elements), every alt prompt (offset shift, plain, reflexive), the controls and each step alone?" && uv run python scripts/pointer_v2.py competence --name d3v2_competence_27b
question: Can Qwen3.6-27B answer pointer_v2's org prompts, every alt prompt (filler moved, filler in place, alt answer also in the org prompt), the 'same' and 'redigit' controls and each step alone (cue -> entity; the lookup with the entity named, or the recalled fact), per topic (animals, elements), family (memory -> prompt, named -> prompt, memory -> memory), type and length (5 statements: 180 scenes per topic; 3 statements: 120)?
why_it_matters: Gate for d3v2_offset_reflexive_main and d3v2_n3: the patching verdicts are only read on scenes the model answers unedited in every family and type. The filler sentence and the digit 0 are new to these prompts. It also says how many prompts per cut remain, which decides whether the rule can be applied per slot (it needs 35 per cut).

hypotheses.H-competent: memory -> prompt clean >= 95% for animals (v1: 98%) and >= 90% for elements (v1: 94%); named -> prompt and memory -> memory >= 98%; >= 70% of scenes eligible in all three families and types for elements, >= 85% for animals
hypotheses.H-filler-hurts: memory -> prompt drops below 85% (Wilson lower bound) in some topic x type cell, so the filler or the locker digit 0 confuses the lookup; that cell is dropped from the patching runs
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-competent 0.75.

decision_rule: pointer_v1's gate, unchanged: a (topic, family, type) cell enters the patching runs iff its clean Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.85; an item is eligible iff every prompt of it is right (org, alt, same, redigit, hop1, hop2); pointer_swap then keeps scenes eligible in every family and type of its run. Report answer-read vs greedy agreement (>= 99%) and, per topic x slot class, the number of eligible scenes (the patching runs need >= 35 per cut).
controls: each step alone (cue -> entity; lookup with the entity named / recalled fact): separates composition failures from missing facts
answer read vs 8-token greedy: validates the one-forward read the patching runs use
n: 5 statements: 180 scenes per topic x 3 families x 3 types (3,240 items); 3 statements: 120 per topic (2,160 items); about 28,600 prompts
notes: Estimate: d3_competence_27b answered 3,360 items (~17,800 prompts) in 1,023 s on this A100 (17 prompts/s); 28,600 prompts -> ~28 min + load. The org prompt, 'same', 'redigit' and the steps are shared by the three types of a scene, so about two thirds of these prompts repeat (kept: the gate reads every item's own prompts).

title: D2 batch 2: do the last tokens read the answer's statement late, through attention, in new locker scenes? (memory → prompt, named → prompt; memory → memory as the null)
command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_pointer_late_read --why "D2 batch 2 (a): the late attention read of the answer's statement on pointer_v1's scenes (animals, elements), memory → prompt and named → prompt vs memory → memory" --dataset pointer_v1 --families RL DL RR --domains animals elements --n 100 --layers all kind bands --sweep path+random --sweep-dests final both --absent && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_pointer_late_read && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_pointer_late_read
examples_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name d2_pointer_late_read --k 3
figures_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py figures --name d2_pointer_late_read
question: On pointer_v1's locker scenes (5 entities, animals and elements), when the last tokens before the answer cannot read the statement giving the answer, does memory → prompt still lose answer org, and does named → prompt (the entity named in the question) too; is the read in layers 48-63 and through attention layers, as on the animal scenes; and does memory → memory stay untouched?
why_it_matters: The first night found, on one animal wording, that the last tokens read the answer's statement themselves, through attention, in layers 48-63, where the bridge is in transit and the lens cannot write it (d2_ko_core_v1 / d2_ko_sweep_v1, UNVERIFIED). D3's pointer patching runs on these pointer_v1 scenes, so the read must be shown where D3 measures. named → prompt is the classic binding retrieval (no recall step): if it reads the statement at the same depth, the late read is the lookup itself, not something that waits for a recalled bridge.

hypotheses.H_late_read: memory → prompt and named → prompt each: the statement giving the answer hidden from the last tokens in all 64 layers keeps answer org <= 40% (NEEDED); hidden only in layers 48-63 <= 60% (NEEDED or PARTIAL); only in 0-31 or only in 32-47 >= 90%; in every attention layer <= 40% (NEEDED); in every DeltaNet layer >= 90%. Prior: memory → prompt 0.65 (animal scenes replicate), named → prompt 0.5
hypotheses.H_named_earlier: named → prompt already needs the statement in layers 32-47 (middle band NEEDED): with the entity named, the lookup can start earlier. Prior 0.3
hypotheses.H_question_free: both lookup families keep >= 90% with the statement hidden from the question words only (animal scenes: 100%). Prior 0.75
hypotheses.H_null: memory → memory: every cell >= 95% (animal scenes: 100%). Prior 0.9
hypotheses.positive_control: every lookup family with the statement hidden from everything after it and removed from the DeltaNet recurrence: <= 30% (5 lockers in the prompt: guessing gives ~20%)

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/attn_knockout.py docstring and manifest "decision"; summary late_attention_read). Items: pointer_v1 main, domains animals and elements (the domains where all three families pass d3_competence_27b's gate: clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85; months fails memory → prompt, planets fails memory → memory), scenes with every competence prompt right in all three families, first 100 per domain by scene id, and unedited read right. A cell is NEEDED if accuracy drops >= 20 points and the paired bootstrap 95% lower bound of acc(same-kind off-path statement) - acc(cell) >= 10 points; NOT NEEDED if the Wilson 95% lower bound of accuracy is >= 90%; else PARTIAL. "Late attention read" holds for a family iff all-layer NEEDED, every-attention-layer NEEDED, every-DeltaNet-layer accuracy >= 90%, layers 48-63 NEEDED or PARTIAL, and layers 0-31 and 32-47 each >= 90%. A family whose positive control is not NEEDED is not interpreted.
controls: a statement of the same kind off the answer's path (another entity's locker, same token length, seeded per scene): rules out "any statement-sized hole breaks the answer"
a random span of the same length inside the statements (never the answer's statement): rules out "any hole in the context"
the up to 3 tokens right after the statement (the DeltaNet conv's reach): what blocking them alone does
memory → memory on the same scenes (the answer is recalled): rules out generic damage to the last tokens
positive control: the statement hidden from everything after it and removed from the DeltaNet recurrence
pre-run check (check.json): an empty source leaves the answer read bit-exact; context independence under full blocking; an unedited row in every batch
n: 175 org prompts per family (animals 96 + elements 79 eligible scenes; every cut per (domain, family) has n >= 79 >= 35, so NOT NEEDED is reachable)
notes: Rows: 47,250 knocked reads (90 per item: 4 destinations x 4 sources at all layers, 4 sources x 2 destinations with the statement removed from the recurrence, and 11 layer sets (the three bands 0-31 / 32-47 / 48-63 each whole, attention-only and DeltaNet-only, every attention layer, every DeltaNet layer) x 2 destinations (last tokens, both) x 3 sources (the statement, the off-path control, the random span)). Measured on this A100 (first night): 33-37 rows/s at ~80-token prompts (pointer_v1: 78) -> ~23 min + load and check ~4 min. 0.8B smoke (qwen35_08b_smoke_d2_pointer_v1, on the box): every stage ran, check.json gates exact (0.0).

title: D3 code: can the 27B answer the Python-code lookups (key named, by list position, through variables, from a cue)?
command: uv run python scripts/code_pointer_v1.py manifest --set main dev --name code_competence_27b --why "D3 code gate: can the 27B run code_pointer_v1's Python lookups (key named, by list position, through a 2- or 3-variable chain, recalled from a cue) and the recall contrast, every alt prompt and each step alone, in chat format?" && uv run python scripts/code_pointer_v1.py competence --name code_competence_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/code_pointer_v1.py examples --name code_competence_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/code_pointer_v1.py figures --name code_competence_27b
question: Can Qwen3.6-27B answer code_pointer_v1's org prompts, the three alt prompts (dissoc, same, redigit) and each step alone, per domain (animals, months), family (named → prompt, list position → prompt, 2-variable chain → prompt, 3-variable chain → prompt, memory → prompt, memory → memory) and size (5 dict entries: all 400 scenes per domain; pilot: 3 and 8 entries, 60 scenes per cell, 8 entries for animals only)?
why_it_matters: Gate for the code version of the D3 dissociation patch (pointer_swap on data/code_pointer_v1/). The prose scenes ("The cow's locker is 5.") read as toy; code is where a pointer is literal (a list index, a variable naming a variable, a dict entry), so a "position" verdict there is the cleanest evidence for the pointer account of the "around" route (C2: the first night found the last tokens carrying the statement slot at 44-50 more often than the entity), and an "identity" or "value" verdict in code would bound it. The patching verdicts are interpretable only on items the model answers unedited, every alt prompt and step included; the list-position and variable-chain families and the dict-lookup-from-a-cue wording are untested on the 27B.

hypotheses.H-code-competent: named → prompt, list position → prompt and 2-variable chain → prompt: org prompt >= 95% in both domains at 5 entries (suite_v1 CODE, a two-dict lookup: 100%; pointer_v1 named → prompt: 100%); 3-variable chain → prompt >= 90%; >= 85% of their items eligible (every prompt right)
hypotheses.H-recall-lookup-animals: memory → prompt (animals) org-prompt Wilson lower bound >= 0.85 (pointer_v1's animals memory → prompt: 98%); memory → memory >= 95% in both domains (pointer_v1: 100%)
hypotheses.H-months-memory-lookup-fails: memory → prompt (months) org prompt < 85% (pointer_v1's months memory → prompt: 46% although each step alone was 100%): then months enter the patching runs without that family
hypotheses.H-more-entries-harder: at 8 entries list position → prompt and 3-variable chain → prompt lose >= 5 points against 5 entries (animals); at 3 entries every family within 2 points of 5
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-code-competent 0.8 (most likely failure: 3-variable chain below 90%, or list position on months); H-recall-lookup-animals 0.75 (risk: "What number does lockers store for the animal known for mooing?" answered with the key, as the 0.8B smoke did); H-months-memory-lookup-fails 0.7; H-more-entries-harder 0.5.

decision_rule: A (domain, family) cell enters the code patching runs iff its org-prompt Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.85 at 5 entries (suite_v1's rule; with n = 400 that needs >= 88% right); an item is eligible iff every prompt of it is right (org, dissoc, same, redigit, hop1, hop2). pointer_swap samples scenes eligible in all of a run's families, so a failing family is dropped from that domain's run rather than shrinking the others. The run is valid only if the answer read agrees with the 8-token greedy answer on >= 99% of prompts per cell. Pilot cells (3 and 8 entries) are reported and never gate a run.
controls: each step alone (hop1: the key alone, i.e. names[i], the chain's last variable, or cue -> key; hop2: the lookup with the key named, or the recalled fact): separates a composition failure from a missing step
named → prompt on the same scene (same dict line, same predictions): the reference every other family is read against
memory → memory on the same code (same dict, a recall question): competence with the code present but unused
answer read vs 8-token greedy: validates the one-forward read the patching runs use
n: Gate cut = one (domain, family) at 5 entries: n = 400 scenes (12 cuts, 4,800 items); pilot cuts n = 60 (18 cuts, 1,080 items, reported only); 33,320 prompts. The later patching runs sample from up to 400 checked scenes per domain, so a per-slot cut (5 slots) keeps n >= 35 for the same-control bound if >= 175 scenes per domain are eligible in all of a run's families.
notes: Greedy, no sampling seeds; item seeds are code_pointer_v1's (5 entries 721, pilot 722). Prompts: 4 per named → prompt item, 6 for the other families (org, 3 alt prompts, 2 steps) = 34 per scene; 2 x 400 x 34 = 27,200 at 5 entries, (2 x 60 + 60) x 34 = 6,120 pilot. Time from a measured rate on this box: d3_competence_27b (pointer_v1, 17,920 prompts of similar length; 62-123 tokens here) took 1,000 s of generate + read = 17.9 prompts/s, so ~1,860 s + model load ~5 min = ~0.6 h; 0.7 h with margin.
