title: D2 batch 2: with the statements in another language (or naming the chemical symbol), do the last tokens still read the answer's statement late, through attention?
command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_alias_late_read --why "D2 batch 2 (c): the late attention read when the statements name the entity in French/Spanish/German (animals) or by its chemical symbol (elements), against the same scenes in English" --dataset alias_pointer_v1 --families RL DL RR --n 60 --layers all kind bands --sweep path+random --sweep-dests final both --absent && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_alias_late_read && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_alias_late_read
examples_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name d2_alias_late_read --k 3
figures_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py figures --name d2_alias_late_read
question: When the statement giving the answer names the entity in another language ("Die Kuh hat den Spind 5.") or by its chemical symbol ("The O card is in locker 5."), while the question stays English, do the last tokens before the answer still read that statement themselves, in layers 48-63, through attention, as they do on the same scenes in English?
why_it_matters: If the late read is a match on the recalled word's token, it should move or weaken when the statement uses another surface form (the token "cow" is not there); if it is a match by meaning, the same late attention read should appear. This decides whether the "around" route is lexical (D3's pointer question, from the D2 side).

hypotheses.H_late_read_english: memory → prompt and named → prompt with English statements: late attention read (all-layer <= 40% NEEDED, layers 48-63 NEEDED or PARTIAL, layers 0-31 and 32-47 >= 90%, every attention layer NEEDED, every DeltaNet layer >= 90%). Prior 0.65
hypotheses.H_late_read_other_surface: the same in the other surface form (French/Spanish/German statements for animals; the chemical symbol for elements). Prior 0.45
hypotheses.H_surface_earlier: in the other surface form the statement is also needed in layers 32-47 (middle band NEEDED): a translation or alias step happens before the fetch. Prior 0.25
hypotheses.H_null: memory → memory in both forms: every cell >= 95%. Prior 0.85
hypotheses.positive_control: every lookup family, both forms, with the statement hidden from everything after it and removed from the DeltaNet recurrence: <= 30%

decision_rule: As d2_pointer_late_read per family and form. Items: alias_pointer_v1 main; a (domain, form, family) cell enters iff its clean Wilson lower bound in alias_competence_27b is >= 0.85 (English) or >= 0.80 (other forms, the builder's gate); a domain enters only if both forms do (scenes paired across forms and families); every competence prompt right; first 60 scenes per (domain, form) by scene id; unedited read right. Comparisons between forms are on the same scenes. A family whose positive control is not NEEDED is not interpreted.
controls: a statement of the same kind off the answer's path (same token length where one exists; length mismatches are flagged in cases.jsonl, likely in the mixed-language animal scenes)
a random span of the same length inside the statements; the up to 3 tokens after the statement
memory → memory in both forms (the answer is recalled)
the English form of the same scenes: the baseline each other-form cell is compared with
positive control and pre-run check as d2_pointer_late_read
n: up to 60 scenes per (domain, form, family): animals in English and in French/Spanish/German, elements in English and with the chemical symbol; each other form exists in one domain only, so its cells have n <= 60 (>= 35 needed for NOT NEEDED; the builder's gate admits forms with >= 25 eligible scenes, below 35 cells are read by accuracy)
notes: Rows: <= 64,800 knocked reads (720 items x 90 conditions). ~79-token prompts at the first night's 33-37 rows/s -> ~32 min + load and check ~4 min. 0.8B smoke (qwen35_08b_smoke_d2_alias_pointer_v1): every stage ran, check.json gates exact (0.0).

title: D3b: does a fitted statement-slot direction steer the lookup where the lens push cannot?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py run --name d3b_slot_direction_main_27b --why "D3b: fit a statement-slot direction at the tokens after the question (layers 40-52) on the fit scenes, steer held-out scenes with it at the alt-prompt patch's size, against the lens push, a random push, a shuffled-label direction and memory → memory items"
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py examples --name d3b_slot_direction_main_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py figures --name d3b_slot_direction_main_27b
question: In memory → prompt on Qwen3.6-27B, does adding a direction fitted to "the asked statement is slot j" (minus the current slot) at the tokens after the question, layers 44-52, switch the answer to the digit at slot j, where the lens push (bridge alt − bridge org) of the same size does not?
why_it_matters: D3 found that at layers 44-50 the last tokens carry which statement slot is asked more often than which entity (29% vs 9%), and the lens cannot steer there. If a fitted slot direction steers the lookup, the "around" route is a statement pointer the model reads, outside the lens's word directions (supports C2's explanation); if it does not, D3's slot answers came from the whole patch, not a linear slot code.

hypotheses.H-slot: slot direction at layer 48, 1x: the answer at the target slot on >= 40% of memory → prompt items (Wilson lower bound >= 30%), lens push <= 10% and random <= 5% at the same size; shuffled-label direction <= 5%; memory → memory <= 5%; held-out entities within 15 points of seen ones; rank-4 subspace within 10 points of the full direction; slot decodable from the last tokens at 44-50 (5-way cross-validated accuracy >= 60%, chance 20%); slot directions no closer to the entities' lens word directions than random (largest |cos| at the null) and their lens-readable share at the random-dictionary null
hypotheses.H-no-linear-slot: slot direction <= 15% at every layer and size 0.5-2x (4x may only break answers); decodability may still be high (readable but not used)
hypotheses.H-illusion: the slot direction passes, but the remainder outside real activation differences alone reaches >= half of its rate while the in-span part stays below half, or the shuffled-label direction also moves >= 10%
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-slot 0.35, H-no-linear-slot 0.5, H-illusion 0.15.

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/pointer_fit.py's docstring and manifest. Primary cell: memory → prompt, animals and elements pooled, all held-out items, slot direction (per-token difference of class means, target minus current slot) at layer 48, 1x the alt-prompt patch's per-token size, added at every token after the question. "The slot direction steers the lookup where the lens push does not" iff (a) its rate of answers at the target slot has a Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.30 and (b) it is >= 20 points above both the lens push and the random push at the same size, with each difference's paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0. Valid only if the shuffled-label direction (memory → prompt) and the slot direction on memory → memory both keep their Wilson upper bound <= 0.10. Illusion flag reported with the verdict. Every other layer, size, subspace rank, the held-out-entity cut and the geometry are reported, not decisive.
controls: random push per token at the same size (rules out any push of that size)
lens push bridge alt − bridge org at the same size (the comparison the claim is about)
shuffled-label direction: the same fit with slot labels permuted (rules out a direction that works without slot information)
memory → memory items: no lookup, so a slot pointer should do nothing (rules out generic answer damage)
held-out scenes (main set; fit on the separate fit set) and held-out entities (queried entity never queried in the fit)
span of real activation differences vs the remainder, each added alone (Makelov et al. 2023 illusion check)
alt-prompt patch at the same tokens and layers (reference: D3's 29% slot answers)
n: memory → prompt: 175 held-out items (animals 96 + elements 79 eligible; >= 35 for every pooled cut, ~85 in the held-out-entity cut); memory → memory: 100 (50 per domain, >= 35); fit: up to 400 fit items, about half kept after the answered-right and fitting-half filters
notes: Timing from the measured A100 rate for the 27B (31-37 edited reads/s): memory → prompt 175 x (1 + 6 layer settings x (4 sizes x 11 conditions + 1 patch)) = 47.4k reads, memory → memory 100 x (1 + 6 x (4 x 4 + 1)) = 10.3k: ~57.7k reads ~ 28 min; + collect (400 forwards) and fit ~1 min, geometry ~2 min, load ~4 min, per-item overhead ~3 min: ~0.7 h. Layers 40-52 are past the first third of the depth. Results: results/pointer_fit/d3b_slot_direction_main_27b/.

title: D2 batch 2: in Python code (dict lookups, list positions, variable chains), do the last tokens still read the answer's dict entry late, through attention?
command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_code_late_read --why "D2 batch 2 (b): the late attention read of the answer's dict entry in code_pointer_v1 programs (named key, list position, 2- and 3-variable chains, recalled key; recalled fact as the null)" --dataset code_pointer_v1 --families DK IX CH2 CH3 RK RR --domains animals months --n 60 --layers all kind bands --sweep path+random --sweep-dests final both --absent && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_code_late_read && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_code_late_read
examples_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name d2_code_late_read --k 3
figures_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py figures --name d2_code_late_read
question: In code_pointer_v1's programs (lockers = {"cow": 5, ...} then a print whose key is named, read from a list position, passed through a 2- or 3-variable chain, or recalled from a cue), when the last tokens before the answer cannot read the dict entry giving the answer, is answer org lost; is the read in layers 48-63 and through attention; and does the recalled-fact family (memory → memory) stay untouched?
why_it_matters: Tests whether the late attention read found on prose locker scenes is how this model does lookups in general or a property of the "The cow's locker is 5." wording. In code the pointer is literal (a list index, a variable naming a variable): if the entry is still read late by the last tokens, the "around the J-space" lookup is a generic late fetch; if the chains move it earlier (or into the print line), the depth of the read depends on how the key is found.

hypotheses.H_late_read: every lookup family (named key, list position, 2-variable chain, 3-variable chain, recalled key): the entry hidden from the last tokens in all 64 layers <= 40% (NEEDED); only in layers 48-63 <= 60% (NEEDED or PARTIAL); only in 0-31 or only in 32-47 >= 90%; in every attention layer <= 40%; in every DeltaNet layer >= 90%. Prior 0.45 (the print line may read the entry itself)
hypotheses.H_question_free: every lookup family keeps >= 90% with the entry hidden from the question words only (here the question words include the print line, e.g. print(lockers[names[0]])). Prior 0.45
hypotheses.H_chain_earlier: the 3-variable chain needs the entry in layers 32-47 already (middle band NEEDED). Prior 0.3
hypotheses.positive_control: every lookup family with the entry hidden from everything after it and removed from the DeltaNet recurrence: <= 30% (5 entries)

decision_rule: As d2_pointer_late_read (NEEDED / NOT NEEDED / PARTIAL per cell against a same-kind off-path entry; "late attention read" per family by the same five conditions). Items: code_pointer_v1 main, domains animals and months; a (domain, family) cell enters iff its clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85 in code_competence_27b; scenes with every competence prompt right in all entered families of the domain; first 60 per domain by scene id; unedited read right. A family whose positive control is not NEEDED is not interpreted.
controls: another dict entry of the same token length off the answer's path (seeded per scene)
a random span of the same length inside the dict line (never the answer's entry; never the list or chain lines, which are on the path)
the up to 3 tokens right after the entry (the DeltaNet conv's reach)
memory → memory (code) on the same programs: the answer is recalled
positive control and pre-run check as d2_pointer_late_read
n: up to 60 programs per (domain, family) after the gate, 120 per family pooled over the two domains (>= 35 per cut if at least 35 scenes per domain are eligible; cells below 35 can not reach NOT NEEDED and are read by accuracy)
notes: Rows: <= 64,800 knocked reads (720 items x 90 conditions, if every family passes the gate). Rate from the first night (33-37 rows/s at ~80 tokens) scaled to code_pointer_v1's 88-token prompts: ~31 rows/s -> ~35 min + load and check ~4 min. 0.8B smoke (qwen35_08b_smoke_d2_code_pointer_v1): every stage ran, check.json gates exact (0.0).

title: D3 with statements in another language or by symbol: does the slot pointer survive when the word differs?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --data alias_pointer_v1 --set main --name d3_alias_main --families RL DL --n 100 --layers 16 20 24 28 32 36 40 42 44 46 48 50 52 54 56 58 60 --groups question final last --question-max-layer 38 --competence alias_competence_27b --why "D3 alias: the three-way patch when the statements name the entity in French/Spanish/German (animals) or by its chemical symbol (elements), on the same scenes as English statements" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_alias_main
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3_alias_main
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py figures --name d3_alias_main
question: When the org prompt's statements name the entities in another language (animals) or by chemical symbol (elements), does patching the alt prompt's tokens after the question still give the answer at the same statement slot as often as with English statements on the same scenes, while the answer of bridge alt's statement (which now needs a translation to find) drops?
why_it_matters: A word-level route (the bridge's word matched against the statement) must translate first; a positional pointer does not care how the statement spells the entity. If the slot answer keeps its share and the word answer drops, the "around" route is a pointer, not a word the lens cannot steer; if both drop, the slot answer was riding on a lexical match.

hypotheses.H-pointer-survives: memory -> prompt, after the question, window 44-52: answer at the same statement slot in the other language within 15 points of English (Newcombe CI, same topic), answer of bridge alt's statement lower by > 15
hypotheses.H-lexical: the slot answer drops by > 15 points with the other language or symbol
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-pointer-survives 0.5, H-lexical 0.3, unclear 0.2.

decision_rule: The pre-registered rule of scripts/pointer_swap.py's docstring per condition; condition contrasts against English in the same topic (the levels' rule of d3_levels_animals_27b): the difference of each outcome's share with a Newcombe 95% interval; 'same' if it lies within ±0.15, 'differs' if it excludes 0 and exceeds 0.15, else unclear; read only if both conditions' cells are interpretable. Primary: memory -> prompt, after the question, window 44-52.
controls: same entity, statements reshuffled: every hypothesis predicts answer org
random push of the same size; a prompt of the other topic, same size
English statements on the same scenes (the reference condition)
org prompt into itself (no-op) and the layer-0 all-position patch (hook checks)
n: up to 100 scenes per topic, each in English and in the alias condition (eligible in both, both families): per (topic x condition x family) up to 100
notes: Depends on alias_competence_27b and d3v2_smoke_27b. ~800 cases x ~139 reads -> ~111k reads at 38/s -> ~50 min.

title: D3 in Python code: does the patched query carry the key, the dict entry's position, or the value?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --data code_pointer_v1 --set main --name d3_code_main --n 100 --layers 16 20 24 28 32 36 40 42 44 46 48 50 52 54 56 58 60 --groups question final last --question-max-layer 38 --competence code_competence_27b --why "D3 code: pointer_v1's three-way patch on Python dict lookups (key named, by list position, through variables, from a recalled cue) and the recall contrast; animals and months, 5 dict entries" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_code_main
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3_code_main
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py figures --name d3_code_main
question: In Python dict lookups (lockers = {"cow": 5, ...}), when the alt program's hidden states at the query and the tokens after it are patched into the org program layer by layer, does the org program answer the value of the alt key's entry (answer of bridge alt's statement), the value at the same entry position (answer at the same statement slot), or the alt program's own answer, for each way the key is found (named, list index, 2- and 3-variable chains, recalled from a cue) and for the recall contrast?
why_it_matters: The animal/locker scenes read as toy. Code has literal pointers (an index, a variable naming another), so if the slot answer of the prose runs is a generic positional pointer it should appear here too, most clearly for the key recalled from a cue (memory -> prompt, the family the lens could read but not steer); if code lookups go by the key's identity instead, the slot result is specific to prose statements.

hypotheses.H-pointer: memory -> prompt (cue -> key), after the query, layers 44-52: answer at the same statement slot (entry position) >= 25%, above the alt key's entry; named -> prompt the same
hypotheses.H-word: answer of bridge alt's statement (the alt key's entry) >= 25%, entry position <= 10%
hypotheses.H-value: the alt program's own answer dominates from layer ~52 (as in prose)
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-pointer 0.45, H-word 0.35, mixed 0.2.

decision_rule: The pre-registered rule of scripts/pointer_swap.py's docstring, unchanged, with the code families' roles: primary = memory -> prompt (RK), reference = named -> prompt (DK), contrast = memory -> memory (RR); list position and the variable chains are reported with the same rule. Primary cell: memory -> prompt, after the query, window 44-52, pooled over topics. Cuts with n < 35 are reported, not judged.
controls: same key at the same entry, the other entries reshuffled and revalued: every hypothesis predicts answer org
random push of the same size; a program of the other topic, same size
context digits no hypothesis predicts
org program into itself (no-op) and the layer-0 all-position patch (hook checks)
n: up to 100 scenes per topic (animals, months; eligible in all six families) -> up to 200 per family pooled; per (topic x family) up to 100; slot cuts (first / last: ~20 per topic) are below 35 and reported only
notes: Depends on code_competence_27b (the code gate) and d3v2_smoke_27b (the --data path on the 27B). If months fail the gate in any family, the scene-level eligibility removes months and n halves. ~1,200 cases x ~139 reads -> ~167k reads at 38/s -> ~75 min.

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_v1.py manifest --set main --name d3b_competence_400 --limit 400 --why "D3b replication gate (batch 3): pointer_v1 main, all 400 scenes per file, so the pointer direction can be tested on scenes the first run never used" && uv run python scripts/pointer_v1.py competence --name d3b_competence_400
question: Which of pointer_v1's 400 main scenes per (domain, family) does Qwen3.6-27B answer right unedited, every prompt of the item (org, alt prompts, each step alone)?

hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: 0.85.

answer read vs 8-token greedy agreement (must be >= 99%)

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_v3.py manifest --name d3_start_or_end_competence_27b --why "D3 start-or-end gate: can the 27B answer pointer_v3's scenes (5 statements and 1-2 filler sentences; the alt prompt has 6 or 4 statements), every alt and control prompt and each step alone, animals and elements?" && uv run python scripts/pointer_v3.py competence --name d3_start_or_end_competence_27b

why_it_matters: Gate for d3_start_or_end_main: its verdicts are read only on scenes answered unedited in every family; the run needs >= 100 usable scenes per topic (pooled over the two alt types) and >= 35 per cut the rule is applied to.

hypotheses.H-competent: memory -> prompt clean >= 95% for animals and >= 90% for elements (pointer_v2 with one filler: 100% and 91%); named -> prompt and memory -> memory >= 98%; usable scenes >= 85% (animals) and >= 65% (elements)
hypotheses.H-two-fillers-hurt: memory -> prompt below 85% (Wilson lower bound) where the org prompt has two filler sentences
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-competent 0.75.

Report read vs greedy agreement on the digit prompts (>= 99%) and the eligible scenes per topic x alt type x slot class.
controls: each step alone (cue -> entity; the lookup with the entity named / the recalled fact)
answer read vs 8-token greedy on the digit prompts
n: 120 scenes per topic x alt type x 3 families = 1,440 items (about 7,600 prompts)
notes: d3v2_competence_27b answered ~28,600 prompts in 1,545 s on the A100 (18.5 prompts/s): ~7 min + load.

command: uv run python scripts/pointer_order.py run --name d3b_order_vs_position_smoke_27b --scene-limit 16 --why "D3b order-or-position smoke: collect, two-fold fit, read test and pushes end to end on 16 scenes before the main run"

title: D3 v2: is the slot the statement's order or its token position, and must the alt answer be in the prompt?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --data pointer_v2 --set main --name d3v2_offset_reflexive_main --families RL DL --n 180 --layers 16 20 24 28 32 36 40 42 44 46 48 50 52 54 56 58 60 --groups question final last --question-max-layer 38 --control-levels e5-pln --competence d3v2_competence_27b --why "D3 v2 main: offset shift (order slot vs token position) and reflexive (alt answer in the org prompt or not) on the same scenes, 5 statements + 1 filler, animals and elements" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3v2_offset_reflexive_main
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3v2_offset_reflexive_main
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py figures --name d3v2_offset_reflexive_main
question: On 5-statement scenes with one filler sentence of a statement's length, when the alt prompt's hidden states at the tokens after the question (and at the last two tokens) are patched into the org prompt at layers 40-60, does the org prompt answer the digit at the same statement ORDER (answer at the same statement slot) or at the same TOKEN position (answer at the same token position)? And is the late "alt prompt's own answer" more common when that digit is also in the org prompt (a pointer to the answer token) than when it is not (the digit carried as content)?
why_it_matters: The first night found that the tokens after the question carry the statement's slot at layers 44-50 (29% vs 9% for the word), but slot order and token position always coincided, and the alt answer was never in the org prompt. If the slot is an order index, the "around" route is a binding ID in the sense of the binding/lookback literature (positional pointers the word lens cannot express); if it is a token position, it is an attention address, closer to D2's finding that the last tokens read the statement through attention at 48-63. If the alt answer needs to be in the prompt, the late phase is a second pointer (reflexive), not the answer carried as a word: either way the lens could read but not write it.

hypotheses.H-order: memory -> prompt, after the question or last two tokens, at the layer of the slot peak (48-50): answer at the same statement slot >= 25% and answer at the same token position <= 10% (offset-shift scenes); verdict "position"
hypotheses.H-token: the same cells: same token position >= 25% and same statement slot <= 10%; verdict "token"
hypotheses.H-both: both >= 10% (verdict "mixed"): the pointer is partly positional in tokens, partly in order
hypotheses.H-reflexive: last two tokens, layers 52-56: the alt answer share with the digit in the org prompt minus without it >= +10 points (paired lower bound)
hypotheses.H-content: the same difference within ±10 points (CI): the digit is carried as content (v1: 98% alt answer at layer 56 though the digit was never in the org prompt)
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-order 0.55, H-token 0.25, H-both 0.2; H-content 0.75, H-reflexive 0.25.

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring, "Decision rule" and "pointer_v2 additions"). Per cell (family x patched tokens x layer or window x alt prompt), pooled over topics, Wilson 95%: interpretable iff the patch changes the answer (lower bound >= 0.20) and the 'same' control changes it rarely (upper bound <= 0.10); the verdict is the outcome whose lower bound exceeds the other candidates' upper bounds and the chance bar (the random push's upper bound, the per-digit rate of unpredicted context digits); offset-shift cells have the candidates {answer of bridge alt's statement, answer at the same statement slot, answer at the same token position, the alt prompt's own answer}. Primary cells: memory -> prompt, offset shift, after the question and last two tokens, layers 48 and 50 and the window 44-52. Reflexive: per cell, the paired (same scene) difference of the alt-answer share, reflexive minus plain, with a paired bootstrap 95% CI: 'reflexive' if the lower bound > +0.10, 'content' if the CI lies within ±0.10, else unclear; read only where the plain cell is interpretable. Every cut the rule is applied to needs n >= 35; cuts below are reported, not judged. A verdict holding in only one of the two topics is reported as topic-dependent.
controls: same entity, statements reshuffled (the "same" alt prompt): every hypothesis predicts answer org; rules out damage
random push of the same size (plain scenes, every 2nd layer of the list): the chance bar for each predicted digit
a prompt of the other topic, same size (plain scenes): realistic-activation null
context digits no hypothesis predicts: chance inside the same runs
plain scenes vs offset-shift scenes on the same org prompts: the slot answer should not move when only the filler moves (if it does, the order/token split is confounded by the filler)
org prompt into itself (no-op) and layer-0 all-position patch (reproduces the alt answer): hook checks
n: up to 180 scenes per topic (all eligible); per (topic x slot class x family x type) about 60 before the gate, expected ~54 (animals) and ~42 (elements) after it if the gate keeps 90% / 70% of scenes; pooled over topics ~96 per slot class and ~290 per family x type. The rule is applied to cuts with n >= 35 only.
notes: Reads per case: 3 checks + question words at 6 layers x 2 alt prompts + after the question and last two tokens at 17 layers x 2 x 2 + windows ((2 sites x 3) + 1) x 2 = 97 (offset, reflexive); plain scenes also get the random push and the other-topic patch at every 2nd layer of the list (3 for the question words, 9 for each other site) x 2 = +42, so 139; ~111 on average. ~1,730 cases (288 eligible scenes x 2 families x 3 types) -> ~192k reads; d3_main_ae_27b ran 92,100 reads in 2,401 s (38/s incl. forwards) -> ~85 min + load -> 1.5 h.

title: D1 at n=80: is the stated bridge carried by its lens-readable part where it is in transit?
command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py parts --name d1_parts_n80_v1 --map d1_map_n80_v1 --why "D1 confirmatory (batch 3): d1_parts_v1 at n=80 per family on d1_map_n80_v1's transit cells, layers 32-52" --lo 32 --sets bind_bridge bridge_word lookup_x context question
examples_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py examples --name d1_parts_n80_v1
figures_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py figures --name d1_parts_n80_v1
question: At the cells where a stated bridge is in transit (prompt → prompt and the tie families on the context at layers 32-44; prompt → memory on its statement at 32-38), how much of the copy's effect does its lens-readable part carry, at n=80 per family instead of 32?
why_it_matters: D1's first-night answer ("for prompt → prompt the lens-readable part of the whole-context paste does 14% of its fair share, null 7%; for prompt → memory 5x") rests on n=32. It is the first claim we would put into VERIFIED.md, so it needs the confirmatory n before a human checks it. It is also the parts input the n=80 lens push (d1_rw_n80_v1) needs.

hypotheses.H-around: at every prompt → prompt statement set in transit at 32-40: concentration upper bound < 1.0 with the rest minus the lens-readable part > 0; prompt → memory (and countries B) at the same sets > 1.2
hypotheses.H-loc: at a prompt → prompt (or tie-family) statement set in transit at 32-40: concentration lower bound > 1.2 and above the random-dictionary null's upper bound
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-around 0.8 (n=32 gave 0.14 [0.10, 0.19] vs null 0.07), H-loc 0.05, inconclusive 0.15.

decision_rule: Unchanged from d1_parts_v1 (statement_positions.py module docstring). Per family, set, primary window (layers 32/36/40 among the transit cells): inside if the J-space concentration (case bootstrap 95%) lower bound > 1.2 and above rand_omp's upper bound; around if the upper bound < 1.0 and not_jspace - jspace > 0 (paired bootstrap lower bound); else inconclusive. H-loc if any prompt → prompt / tie-family statement set is inside; H-around if all are around and the positive control (countries B, else prompt → memory) is inside at the same set; around without a passing positive control is not interpretable.
controls: a random subspace of the same size per cell (the null concentration)
the copy itself at the same cell (the effect to split)
prompt → memory and countries B at the same sets (positive controls: the lens-readable part carries the bridge)
n: 80 per family (d1_map_n80_v1's cases; BL, BR, RL, RR, BLR, BRL, countries R, B), only families with transit cells at layers >= 32
notes: d1_parts_v1 took ~0.35 h at n=32 on one A100; n=80 scales it ~2.5x: ~0.9 h. Results: results/statement_positions/d1_parts_n80_v1/.

title: D3b replication: does the pointer direction steer the lookup on fresh scenes?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py run --name d3b_replicate_fresh_27b --competence d3b_competence_400 --n-test 400 --rr-n 100 --steer-layers 44 48 --scales 1.0 2.0 --ks 4 --why "D3b replication (batch 3): the same fit, steered on every eligible main scene (the primary cell: scenes the first run never used), layers 44 and 48, 1x and 2x"
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py examples --name d3b_replicate_fresh_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py figures --name d3b_replicate_fresh_27b
question: On memory → prompt scenes that d3b_slot_direction_main_27b never used, does the pointer direction (fitted to "which statement the question asks", target minus current) at layer 48, 1x the alt-prompt patch's size, switch the answer to the target statement's digit, where the lens push of the same size does not?

hypotheses.H-replicates: fresh scenes, layer 48, 1x: target-statement answers 30-45%, Wilson lower bound >= 0.30 with n ~500; lens push and random <= 2%; shuffled-label and memory → memory <= 5%
hypotheses.H-regresses: fresh scenes: rate < 30% (the first run's 37% was a lucky draw)
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-replicates 0.6 (the point estimate 37% with n~500 gives a lower bound ~33%), H-regresses 0.4.

decision_rule: Fixed before the run. Primary cell: memory → prompt, animals and elements pooled, held-out main items whose scene index is >= 100 (never used by d3b_slot_direction_main_27b), slot direction at layer 48, 1x, every token after the question; computed from outcomes.jsonl (name suffix >= 0100). Same rule as d3b_slot_direction_main_27b: passes iff the Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.30 and the rate is >= 20 points above both the lens push and the random push at the same size with each paired-bootstrap lower bound > 0; valid only if the shuffled-label direction and the slot direction on memory → memory keep their Wilson upper bound <= 0.10. The script's own verdict (all eligible items, old ones included) is reported next to it, not decisive. Layer 44 and 2x are reported, not decisive.
controls: random push per token at the same size
lens push bridge alt − bridge org at the same size
shuffled-label direction (slot labels permuted before the fit)
memory → memory items (no lookup: the pointer should do nothing)
held-out entities (queried entity never queried in the fit)
in-span part vs remainder (illusion check)
n: memory → prompt: every eligible main item (~380 animals + ~300 elements, of which ~500 fresh); memory → memory: 100 per domain; fit: as d3b_slot_direction_main_27b (fit set, separate scenes)
notes: Reads: ~680 memory → prompt items x (1 + 3 layer settings x (2 sizes x 7 conditions + 1 patch)) = ~31k, memory → memory 200 x 28 = ~5.6k: ~37k reads at 31-37/s ~ 20 min; + collect and fit ~3 min, geometry ~2 min, load ~4 min: ~0.6 h. Results: results/pointer_fit/d3b_replicate_fresh_27b/.

title: D1 at n=80: does the lens push write a stated bridge where it is in transit?
command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py readwrite --name d1_rw_n80_v1 --map d1_map_n80_v1 --parts d1_parts_n80_v1 --why "D1 confirmatory (batch 3): d1_rw_v1 at n=80 per family; resolves the inconclusive 16x cell (3/32 vs 1/32 random)" --lo 32 --sets bind_bridge bridge_word lookup_x context question
examples_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py examples --name d1_rw_n80_v1
figures_command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py figures --name d1_rw_n80_v1
question: At the cells where a stated bridge is in transit (layers 32-44), does pushing along the lens's bridge alt − bridge org direction (0.5-16x the copy's per-position size) switch prompt → prompt answers more than a random push of the same size, at n=80 per family?
why_it_matters: The write half of D1. At n=32 every cell was 0/32 except one 16x cell (3/32 vs 1/32 random) that the rule could not decide. With n=80 "the lens push does not write a stated bridge where it is carried" can be decided (or refuted) at every size, which is what a human needs to put D1 into VERIFIED.md.

hypotheses.H-around: prompt → prompt and the tie families: lens − random switch difference upper bound < 10 points at every size 0.5-16x at every transit cell; countries B / prompt → memory written at the same sets
hypotheses.H-loc: prompt → prompt: lens switches >= 30% at <= 4x with random <= 5% at some transit cell
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-around 0.75; the 16x cell stays below 10 points 0.7 (n=32: +6 points).

decision_rule: Unchanged from d1_rw_v1 (statement_positions.py module docstring): per family, set, primary window: written if at some size <= 4x lens switches >= 30% and the paired-bootstrap lower bound of lens − random > 0; not written if at every size the difference's upper bound < 0.10; else inconclusive. Combined D1 verdict with d1_parts_n80_v1 as in d1_rw_v1.
controls: a random direction per position at the same sizes (rules out a pure size effect)
the copy at the same cell (the effect to explain)
bridge alt's rank at the same positions (the read's floor)
countries B and prompt → memory at the same sets (positive control: written)
n: 80 per family (d1_map_n80_v1's cases), only families with transit cells at layers >= 32
notes: d1_rw_v1 took ~0.2 h at n=32; n=80: ~0.5 h. Results: results/statement_positions/d1_rw_n80_v1/.

title: D3b: does the pointer direction mean "the Nth statement" or "this token position"?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_order.py run --name d3b_order_vs_position_27b --why "D3b order or position: fit the pointer direction on pointer_v2 prompts whose asked statement precedes the filler sentence (the Nth statement = the Nth position), push held-out scenes toward a statement after the filler (the Nth statement now sits one position later), two folds"
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_order.py examples --name d3b_order_vs_position_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_order.py figures --name d3b_order_vs_position_27b
question: When the pointer direction (fitted to "the question asks statement N") is pushed into a scene where a filler sentence has shifted the later statements by one position, does the model answer with the Nth statement's digit (ORDER) or with the digit of whatever statement now sits at position N (TOKEN POSITION)?
why_it_matters: d3b_slot_direction_main_27b found a direction that steers the lookup where the lens push cannot (37% vs 0%), but in pointer_v1 "the Nth statement" and "the Nth token position" are the same thing. ORDER means the "around" route is an ordinal pointer into a list (the binding-ID / lookback picture); TOKEN means it is a positional address, which would not survive any change of layout and points to attention-by-position, not to a variable.

hypotheses.H-order: statements after the filler, layer 48, 2x: answers = the target statement's digit >= 20%, = the digit now at its old position <= 5%; targets before the filler (both readings agree) >= 25%; read test (no push, asked statement after the filler): the fitted read-out picks the statement's number more often than the position one later
hypotheses.H-token: order <= 5%, token >= 20%; the read test picks the position one later
hypotheses.H-both: both >= 10% (the direction carries a mixture, or the two codes coexist)
hypotheses.H-no-transfer: targets before the filler < 15% (the direction does not work in these scenes): not interpretable
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-order 0.45, H-token 0.3, H-both 0.15, H-no-transfer 0.1 (positional binding IDs in the literature are ordinal; but every context here has the same length, so a positional code would also have been sufficient for the model).

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/pointer_order.py's docstring and manifest. Primary cut: memory → prompt, held-out scenes whose asked statement comes before the filler, targets after it (separating), slot push (target minus current) at layer 48, 2x the alt-prompt patch's per-token size. order = share of answers = the target statement's digit, token = share = the digit of the statement that now sits at the target's position; order - token by a scene-cluster bootstrap (2000, seed 0). ORDER iff order - token has its 95% lower bound > 0, order >= 2 x token and order's Wilson lower bound >= 0.10; TOKEN iff the reverse; BOTH iff both Wilson lower bounds >= 0.10 and neither; else inconclusive. Valid only if targets before the filler land on the target statement with Wilson lower bound >= 0.15, the random push and the shuffled-label direction land on either predicted digit with Wilson upper bound <= 0.10, and the slot push changes memory → memory answers with Wilson upper bound <= 0.10 (each n >= 35). Filler-position targets, scenes whose asked statement follows the filler, the push without the current statement, layer 44, 1x, both layers and the read test are reported, not decisive.
controls: random push per token at the same size (rules out any push of that size)
shuffled-label direction (rules out a direction that works without statement information)
memory → memory items: nothing is looked up, so a pointer should change nothing
targets before the filler: both readings agree there (positive control: the direction works in pointer_v2 at all)
targets at the filler's position: the order reading predicts the target digit, the token reading the filler (no digit)

push without the current statement (target minus the mean): neutral between the readings; the primary subtracts the current statement, which is the same under both readings only when it precedes the filler (hence the primary cut)
two folds: every scene is steered by a fit that never saw it
n: memory → prompt: 287 eligible scenes (animals 180, elements 107). Primary cut: 125 separating target instances in 55 scenes (animals 77, elements 48), >= 35; positive control 392 instances (122 scenes); memory → memory 287 scenes x 4 targets; read test 59 scenes whose asked statement follows the filler; fit 367 + 363 prompts (two folds)
notes: Timing: 287 memory → prompt scenes x 97 rows + 287 memory → memory x 49 = ~41.9k edited reads at 31-37/s ~19-23 min, + collect (~730 fit prompts and 2 forwards per scene) ~1 min, load ~4 min, overhead ~3 min: ~0.5 h. Related: d3v2_offset_reflexive_main (running) asks the same question with the alt-prompt patch instead of a fitted direction. A stronger version needs a data change (see the agent report): a pointer_v2 fit set with the filler always last and a steer set with it always first, so every target after statement 1 separates the readings. Results: results/pointer_order/d3b_order_vs_position_27b/.

title: D3b: can the last tokens tell which statement the question asks about, with twice the data?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_probe.py run --name d3b_slot_probe_27b --why "D3b probe re-analysis (batch 3): read the asked statement from the tokens after the question with the nearest per-statement mean, cross-validated on all 400 fit scenes, layers 40-52, and with the first run's own means on entities it never saw"
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_probe.py examples --name d3b_slot_probe_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_probe.py figures --name d3b_slot_probe_27b
question: With all 400 pointer_v1 fit scenes (animals and elements) instead of 197, can a nearest per-statement-mean read-out of the tokens after the question tell which of the 5 statements the question asks about at layer 48, and is the first run's 39% (steers but hardly readable) a small-sample effect?
why_it_matters: d3b_slot_direction_main_27b read the asked statement at only 39% [33, 46] yet steered with the same means (37%). If more data makes it readable (>= 60%), the pointer is an ordinary readable code and its low read-out was noise; if it stays low, the model carries a pointer that a push can use but a simple read-out barely sees, which matters for any "pointer lens" built from read-outs.

hypotheses.H-readable: layer 48, cross-validated, all items (n ~ 400): Wilson lower bound >= 0.60; answered-right items higher still; the first run's own means on entities it never saw >= 50%
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-hardly-readable 0.6, in between 0.25, H-readable 0.15 (twice the data helps a nearest-mean read-out only modestly when each class mean averages ~80 items over ~20 tokens x 5120 dimensions).

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/pointer_probe.py's docstring and manifest. At layer 48, 5-fold cross-validated nearest-class-mean accuracy on all fit scenes: "readable" iff its Wilson 95% lower bound >= 0.60; "hardly readable" (the first run's 39% survives) iff its upper bound < 0.60; otherwise in between. Valid only if the shuffled-label null stays within 10 points of chance (20%). Per layer (40-52), per topic, answered-right items and the first run's own means on held-out entities are reported, with an entity-cluster bootstrap (queried entities within topic).
controls: shuffled labels (same classifier and folds): must sit at chance
the first run's own class means applied to entities it never saw (out of sample for those means)
per topic and answered-right-only cuts
n: all pointer_v1 fit scenes for animals and elements: 400 (200 per topic, 22 queried entities); answered right ~half (the first run kept 197 of 400 with its entity filter)
notes: Timing: 400 forwards (no edits) ~1 min, cross-validation over 7 layers ~2 min, load ~4 min: ~0.15 h. Needs the first run's cached means (cache/pointer_fit/d3b_slot_direction_main_27b/fits.pt, present on the 4xA100 box); without them the same-means check is skipped and the rest runs. Results: results/pointer_probe/d3b_slot_probe_27b/.

title: D3: is the statement-slot pointer counted from the start or from the end of the list (or is it a token position)?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --data pointer_v3 --set main --name d3_start_or_end_main --families RL DL --n 120 --layers 40 42 44 46 48 50 52 54 56 --groups final last --competence d3_start_or_end_competence_27b --why "D3 start or end: alt prompts with one statement more or fewer, so the slot counted from the start, the slot counted from the end and the same token position name three different org statements; animals and elements" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3_start_or_end_main
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3_start_or_end_main
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py figures --name d3_start_or_end_main
question: When the alt prompt has one statement more (or fewer) than the org prompt and its hidden states at the last two tokens (and at every token after the question) are patched into the org prompt at layers 40-56, does the org prompt answer the digit of the statement at the same place counted from the START of the list, counted from the END, at the same TOKEN position, the answer of bridge alt's statement, or the alt prompt's own answer?
why_it_matters: The pointer found at layers 44-50 (the slot answer beats the word) could be an index from the start of the list (a binding ID as in the lookback literature), an index from the end (recency, as attention to the latest bindings), or an address in the token sequence. With equal list lengths all three coincided. Which one it is decides what a "pointer readout" must read, and whether the lens's failure to steer is about indices or about attention addresses.

hypotheses.H-start: memory -> prompt, last two tokens, layer 50 (and after the question, layer 48): answer at the same slot counted from the start >= 25% and counted from the end <= 10%, in both alt types
hypotheses.H-end: counted from the end >= 25% and from the start <= 10%, in both alt types
hypotheses.H-token: the same token position >= 25%, both slot answers <= 10% (would agree with a token-position result of d3v2_offset_reflexive_main)
hypotheses.H-mixed: two of them >= 10% (verdict "mixed"), or the winner differs between one more and one fewer
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-start 0.4, H-token 0.25, H-end 0.15, H-mixed 0.2.

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring, "Decision rule" and "pointer_v3 additions"). Per cell (family x patched tokens x layer or window x alt type), pooled over topics, Wilson 95%: interpretable iff the patch changes the answer (lower bound >= 0.20) and the same-entity control changes it rarely (upper bound <= 0.10); the verdict is the outcome among {answer of bridge alt's statement, slot from the start, slot from the end, same token position, the alt prompt's own answer} whose lower bound exceeds the others' upper bounds and the random push's upper bound; else "mixed". Primary cells: memory -> prompt, last two tokens and after the question, layers 48 and 50 and the window 44-52; the answer counts only if it holds for both alt types, else it is type-dependent. Every cut needs n >= 35; cuts below are reported, not judged.
controls: same entity, statements reshuffled (same filler places): every hypothesis predicts answer org
random push of the same size (every 2nd layer): chance bar for each predicted digit
a prompt of the other topic, same size: realistic-activation null
org prompt into itself (no-op) and the layer-0 all-position patch (hook checks)
both alt types: an artefact of one filler arrangement should not appear in both
n: up to 120 scenes per topic x alt type (all eligible): per (topic x alt type x family) ~115 (animals) and ~80 (elements) if the gate keeps 96% / 68% as for pointer_v2, i.e. >= 100 per topic pooled over the alt types; per alt type pooled over topics ~195. Slot cuts (first / middle / last, 40 each before the gate) fall below 35 for elements alone and are judged only pooled over topics.
notes: Reads per case: 3 checks + 9 layers x 2 sites x 2 (alt, same) + random/other at 5 layers x 2 sites x 2 + 3 windows x 2 sites x 2 = 71; ~790 cases (395 eligible scenes x 2 families) -> ~56k reads at 34/s -> ~28 min + forwards and load (~10 min) -> 0.7 h. Separability: one statement more or fewer shifts the alt list's indices, and the filler cells (1-2 per prompt, each a statement's length) are placed so that the start-counted slot, the end-counted slot and the token position always name three different org statements (checked per item by pointer_v3 check).

title: D3 v4 entity check: which countries, sports, animals and body parts can the 27B recall from a cue?

question: For each candidate entity of pointer_v4 (countries: cue "the country whose capital is Lima", fact the first digit of the dialling code; sports: "the sport played with a puck", players per side; animals: "the animal known for hooting", legs; body parts (backup): "the body part that makes urine", how many a human has), does Qwen3.6-27B answer the cue -> entity, entity -> fact and cue -> fact prompts right, with no context?

Entities are picked by this gate, not by guess: an entity the model cannot recall would put recall failures, not pointer effects, into every scene it appears in.

hypotheses.H-countries: cue -> entity >= 34/36; dialling-code first digit (fact and chain) >= 28/36: countries usable
hypotheses.H-sports: cue -> entity >= 18/23; players per side right for the team sports and "1" for most individual sports: >= 16 pass, sports usable; otherwise body parts replace sports
hypotheses.H-animals: pointer_v1's 16 pass (they did in d3_competence_27b); >= 30/40 pass in all

The split (a seeded third of each pool and the third wording held out of every fit) is drawn at make from the passing entities only.
controls: three prompts per entity: a fact the model knows only for the named entity fails "chain"; a cue it cannot resolve fails "cue"
pointer_v1's 16 animals, which the 27B answered in d3_competence_27b, as a known-good reference
n: 120 candidate entities x 3 prompts = 360 prompts

title: D3 v2 with 3 statements: order or token position, when bridge alt is not in the org prompt
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --data pointer_v2 --set n3 --name d3v2_n3 --families RL DL --n 120 --layers 16 20 24 28 32 36 40 42 44 46 48 50 52 54 56 58 60 --groups question final last --question-max-layer 38 --control-levels e3-pln --competence d3v2_competence_27b --why "D3 v2 secondary level: 3 statements + 1 filler; bridge alt is not in the org prompt, so the slot answers (order vs token position) compete only with the alt answer" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3v2_n3
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3v2_n3
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py figures --name d3v2_n3
question: With 3 statements and one filler sentence (bridge alt not in the org prompt), does the patch from the alt prompt give the answer at the same statement slot, at the same token position, or the alt prompt's own answer, by layer; and does the reflexive contrast agree with the 5-statement run?

With bridge alt absent from the org prompt, the word cannot be looked up there at all, so any slot answer is a pointer by construction. It is the secondary level of the v2 test (fewer statements: Mixing Mechanisms predicts more positional binding).

hypotheses.H-order: memory -> prompt, after the question, layer 48: answer at the same statement slot >= 40%, same token position <= 10%
hypotheses.H-token: same token position >= 40%, same statement slot <= 10%
hypotheses.H-reflexive: last two tokens, 52-56: alt answer share with the digit in the org prompt minus without >= +10 points

Primary cells: memory -> prompt, offset shift, after the question and last two tokens, layers 48 and 50 and the window 44-52. The query sits first or last only (one filler cell shifts a statement by one cell, so with the query in the middle the token-pointed statement would be the query itself).
controls: same entity, statements reshuffled: every hypothesis predicts answer org
random push of the same size and a prompt of the other topic (plain scenes)
context digits no hypothesis predicts
org prompt into itself (no-op) and the layer-0 all-position patch (hook checks)

Report read vs greedy agreement on the digit prompts and the eligible scenes per topic, per wording and per held-out cut.
controls: each step alone (cue -> entity with the context; the lookup with the entity named / the recalled fact)
answer read vs 8-token greedy on the digit prompts

title: D3b fair test of C2: where the lens reads the word (layers 32-40), does a pointer push steer the lookup that the lens push cannot?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fair.py run --name d3b_fair_c2_27b --why "D3b fair C2 (batch 3): the pointer direction and the lens push at the same size, aimed at the same digit, at read_write's cell (layers 32-40, the tokens after the cue) and at the question words; named → prompt and prompt → prompt as other lookups, memory → memory as the null"
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fair.py examples --name d3b_fair_c2_27b
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fair.py figures --name d3b_fair_c2_27b
question: At layers 32-40, on the tokens after the cue (where the J-lens reads the recalled bridge 95% of the time but its push switches <= 3% of memory → prompt answers), does a fitted pointer push toward bridge alt's statement switch the answer to that statement's digit, where the lens push toward bridge alt, of the same size and aimed at the same digit, does not?
why_it_matters: C2 says the lens cannot write a lookup-used bridge where the model carries it. d3b_slot_direction_main_27b showed a pointer code that steers the lookup at layer 48, not at the depth where read-without-write was measured. If the pointer also steers at 32-40 (and the lens push does not), "around the lens" is explained at the very cell C2 was stated for; if it does not, the pointer forms later (44-50) and at 32-40 the lookup is carried by something neither push reaches.

hypotheses.H-pointer-at-lens-depth: deciding cell (memory → prompt, after the cue, layers 32-40 at once, 1x): pointer push >= 40% to bridge alt's statement digit (entity-bootstrap lower bound >= 30%), lens push <= 5%, random <= 2%, shuffled labels <= 5%; memory → memory answers changed <= 5%
hypotheses.H-pointer-later-only: deciding cell: pointer push < 15% at every size 0.5-2x (D3 found statement-slot answers only at layers 44-50; at 32-40 the last tokens may not carry the pointer yet); the alt-prompt patch there also mostly keeps answer org
hypotheses.H-overshoot: secondary: among the pointer push's off-target answers, more land beyond the target (far side from the asked statement) than a uniform choice predicts, and more than under the shuffled-label direction
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-pointer-at-lens-depth 0.3, H-pointer-later-only 0.55, other (both weak, or the lens push also moves the answer when aimed at a statement digit) 0.15; H-overshoot 0.6 if the pointer moves answers at all.

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/pointer_fair.py's docstring and manifest. Deciding cell: memory → prompt, the tokens after the cue (the question's last token and everything after it: read_write's cell), layers 32, 36 and 40 at once, 1x the alt-prompt patch's per-token size, topics pooled. Pass iff the pointer push's rate of answers = bridge alt's statement digit has an entity-bootstrap 95% lower bound >= 0.30 and exceeds both the lens push and the random push by >= 20 points with each paired entity-bootstrap lower bound > 0. Valid only if the shuffled-label direction stays at an upper bound <= 0.10 and the pointer push changes memory → memory answers with an upper bound <= 0.10 (n >= 35 each). Second deciding cell, same rule: memory → prompt, the question words, layers 32-40 at once, 1x. Reported, not decisive: each layer, each size, per topic, named → prompt, prompt → prompt. Secondary (pre-registered from an exploratory post-hoc pattern): overshoot iff the off-target answers' share beyond the target exceeds the uniform expectation with an entity-bootstrap lower bound > 0.
controls: lens push bridge alt − bridge org, same size, aimed at the same digit (the comparison C2 is about)
random push per token at the pointer push's size
shuffled-label direction (same fit, statement labels permuted): a direction without statement information
memory → memory items: nothing is looked up, so a pointer should change nothing
alt-prompt patch at the same tokens and layers (reference)
held-out scenes (pointer_v1 main; fit on the fit set) and held-out entities (queried entity outside the fitting half)
n: memory → prompt: up to 150 per topic (300; d3b_competence_400 gate, ~380 animals and ~300 elements eligible), 22 queried entities; named → prompt and memory → memory: 100 per topic; prompt → prompt: 400 animal-suite scenes, 200 fit and 200 pushed. Each cut >= 35 items; per topic >= 100 for memory → prompt.
notes: Timing: 300 x 137 + 600 x 69 = ~82.5k edited reads at 31-37/s ~37-44 min, + fit collect (400 + 200 forwards) ~1 min, load ~4 min, overhead ~5 min: ~0.9 h. "After the cue" = the question's last token ("?") and the instruction, template and "Answer:" after it: read_write's question group (its first token is one later for memory → prompt items, read_write starting right after the cue). Results: results/pointer_fair/d3b_fair_c2_27b/.

title: D3b v4: does the fitted pointer direction steer the lookup for entities and wordings the fit never saw?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py run --data pointer_v4 --name d3v4_fit_main --competence d3v4_competence_27b --n-test 150 --rr-n 50 --steer-layers 44 46 48 50 52 --scales 1.0 2.0 --ks 4 --why "D3b on pointer_v4: fit the statement-slot direction on the fit set (fit entities and wordings only), steer main items whose asked entity or wording is held out, entity-cluster intervals"
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py examples --name d3v4_fit_main
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fit.py figures --name d3v4_fit_main
question: On pointer_v4, does adding the direction fitted to "the asked statement is slot j" minus the current slot (per token, at every token after the question, layer 48, 1x the alt-prompt patch's size) switch the answer to the digit at slot j on memory -> prompt items whose asked entity or wording was held out of the fit, where the lens push of the same size does not?
why_it_matters: D3b's first run passed by 0.3 points on item-level intervals (37% [30.3, 45], 22 entities, one wording) and failed on an entity-cluster interval ([28.7, 45.2]). pointer_v4 tests the same claim with ~3x the entities, three wordings, a recorded held-out split (the fit never sees a test entity or wording) and entity-cluster intervals as the primary. A pass makes "a pointer direction the lens cannot express steers the lookup" a candidate for VERIFIED.md; a fail on held-out items says the direction was fitted to the entities or the sentence frame.

hypotheses.H-slot: slot direction, layer 48, 1x, pooled held-out items: target-slot answers 30-45%, entity-cluster lower bound >= 0.30, >= 20 points above the lens push and the random push (cluster lower bounds of both differences > 0); shuffled-label direction and memory -> memory <= 5%
hypotheses.H-held-out-drop: the held-out-entity cut is >= 15 points below the held-out-wording cut (the direction carries entity-specific content), or the rate is < 0.30 pooled
hypotheses.H-topic: the rate differs by > 20 points between topics (pointer_v1: animals vs elements)
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-slot passes the rule 0.35; H-held-out-drop 0.3; H-topic 0.35.

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/pointer_fit.py's docstring ("Decision rule" and "pointer_v4 additions") and the manifest. Primary cell: memory -> prompt, topics pooled, every steered item (asked entity or wording held out of the fit), slot direction at layer 48, 1x. Passes iff (a) its target-slot rate's entity-cluster 95% lower bound (asked entity resampled within each topic, 2000 resamples, seed 0, widened to Wilson where wider) >= 0.30 and (b) it is >= 20 points above both the lens push and the random push at the same size, each difference's entity-cluster bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0. Valid only if the shuffled-label direction and the slot direction on memory -> memory keep their upper bound <= 0.10 (n >= 35 each). Illusion flag reported with the verdict. Reported, not decisive: item-level intervals, per topic, per held-out cut (entity / wording / both), n items / k entities / t wordings, other layers and 2x, the rank-4 subspace, geometry.
controls: random push per token at the same size
lens push bridge alt − bridge org at the same size (the comparison the claim is about)
shuffled-label direction (slot labels permuted before the fit)
memory -> memory items (no lookup: a pointer should do nothing)
held-out split recorded in data/pointer_v4/split.json: test entities and the third wording never in the fit
in-span part vs remainder (illusion check)
alt-prompt patch at the same tokens and layers (reference)
n: memory -> prompt: up to 150 eligible held-out items per topic (~420-450 pooled over ~70-100 asked entities; sports may have ~130 after the gate); memory -> memory: 50 per topic; fit: up to 200 fit scenes per topic (~570), those answered right kept
notes: Reads: memory -> prompt ~450 x (1 + 6 layer settings x (2 sizes x 7 conditions + 1 patch)) = ~41k, memory -> memory 150 x (1 + 6 x (2 x 4 + 1)) = ~8.3k: ~49k reads at 31-37/s ~ 24 min; + collect ~570 forwards and fit ~2 min, geometry ~2 min, load ~4 min: ~0.6 h. The conditions match d3b_replicate_fresh_27b (sizes 1x and 2x, rank 4) with all five steer layers. Results: results/pointer_fit/d3v4_fit_main/.

title: D2 batch 3: in Python code, which later lines read the answer's dict entry? (the names list, each chain line, the print line, the last tokens, and their unions)
command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_code_readers --why "D2 batch 3 (b): the answer's dict entry hidden from one later code line at a time (names list, chain lines, print line, rest of the question, last tokens) and from unions with the last tokens, all layers, on code_pointer_v1 (animals, months)" --dataset code_pointer_v1 --families DK IX CH2 CH3 RK --domains animals months --n 100 --grid code_readers && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_code_readers && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_code_readers
examples_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name d2_code_readers --k 3
figures_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py figures --name d2_code_readers
question: In code_pointer_v1 (lockers = {"bee": 7, ..., "mouse": 5}; names = ["mouse", ...]; print(lockers[names[0]]) -> 5), batch 2 found (UNVERIFIED) that hiding the answer's dict entry from the last tokens in all layers leaves 36% of list-position programs right (43/120), from the question words (print line onward) 100%, from everything after the entry 3%. Which later lines read the entry themselves: the names list line, a chain line (x = "mouse"), the print line, the rest of the question? Does a line pass it on, i.e. does hiding it from that line and the last tokens together cost more than the last tokens alone, and do these lines account for the gap between 36% and 3%?
why_it_matters: The late read by the last tokens is D2's main finding; the 36% that survive it in list-position code say the entry also reaches the answer another way. If the names list line (which contains "mouse") reads the entry and relays it, the model pre-fetches values at the key's mention, a different mechanism from the late lookup, and the J-space question then applies to the list tokens, not only the last ones. The named-key family is the code analogue of named → prompt's early read at the question words (here: the key literal in the print line).

hypotheses.H_print_reader: named key: the print line (print(lockers["mouse"])) is a reader of the entry (batch 2: the question words, which start at the print line, are needed: 6% kept). Prior 0.8
hypotheses.H_list_not_reader: list position: the names list line alone is not a reader (the last tokens still read the entry directly). Prior 0.6
hypotheses.H_relay: list position: the names list line (or the print line) relays the entry: blocking it together with the last tokens costs >= 10 points more than the last tokens alone. Prior 0.65
hypotheses.H_explained: in every family, the union (last tokens + print line + list/chain lines + the rest of the question) keeps answer org within 10 points of hiding the entry from every line after the dict, i.e. no other line (the other chain, the closing fence) matters. Prior 0.55

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/attn_knockout.py BATCH3_RULES and INTERVALS, written into manifest.json). Items: code_pointer_v1 main, animals and months, the (domain, family) cells passing code_competence_27b's gate (clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85; months fails it for the recalled key), scenes with every competence prompt right in every entered family, first 100 per domain by scene id, unedited read right. The entry is hidden (attention scores masked, DeltaNet values removed, all 64 layers) from: the names list line; each chain line by role (the key's chain, lines 1-3; the other chain); the print line; the rest of the question (closing fence, English question, instruction); the last tokens; the unions last tokens + print, + list/chain lines, + both, + both + the rest of the question; every line after the dict; everything after the entry. A line is a READER if acc(control) - acc(line) >= 10 points with the 95% entity-cluster bootstrap lower bound >= 5 points (control: another dict entry of the same token length hidden from the same line, same items). A line RELAYS if adding it to the last tokens' block costs >= 10 more points than the last tokens alone (entity-cluster lower bound >= 5). The lines EXPLAIN the survivors if the full union is within 10 points of "every line after the dict" (point estimate). Intervals: entity-cluster bootstrap (queried keys resampled within domain: 12 animals, 7 months; 4,000 draws, seed 0) first, item level second; every number per domain with n items / k keys. n per cut: 100 per domain (>= 35).
controls: another dict entry (same token length, seeded per scene) hidden from the same line or union: every reader and relay is measured against it
everything after the entry (the positive control of batch 2: 3% kept in list position)
the last tokens alone (reproduces batch 2: 36% in list position)
pre-run check (check.json): an empty source leaves the answer read bit-exact; context independence under full blocking
n: 900 programs (named key, list position, 2- and 3-variable chains: 100 animals + 100 months each; recalled key: 100 animals; months fails the gate for it)
notes: Rows: 19,000 knocked reads (per program: 7 destinations for named key, 10 list position, 13 two-variable chain, 15 three-variable chain, 5 recalled key; x 2 sources). Code prompts are ~92 tokens: measured ~28 reads/s -> ~11 min + load and check ~5 min. Local 0.8B CPU smoke (qwen35_08b_smoke_d2_code_cpu1, scratchpad): every stage ran, check.json gates exact; the line destinations decode to the intended lines (tokenizer check). Results: results/attn_knockout/d2_code_readers/.

title: D3 v4: with many more entities and wordings, does the patch still carry bridge alt's statement slot rather than its word or answer?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py manifest --data pointer_v4 --set main --name d3v4_swap_main --n 150 --layers 16 24 32 40 44 46 48 50 52 56 --groups final last --competence d3v4_competence_27b --why "D3 v4 main: D3's word / slot / answer patch on pointer_v4 (three topics of >= 16 probe-passing entities, three wordings), 150 eligible scenes per topic, entity-cluster intervals" && uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py run --name d3v4_swap_main
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py examples --name d3v4_swap_main
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_swap.py figures --name d3v4_swap_main
question: On pointer_v4 (5 statements; three topics with >= 16 entities each and three statement and question wordings), when the alt prompt's hidden states at the tokens after the question (or the last two tokens) are patched into the org prompt at layers 44-52, does the org prompt answer the digit of bridge alt's statement (its word), the digit at the same statement slot (a pointer), or the alt prompt's own answer, with intervals that resample entities?
why_it_matters: D3's slot answer at 44-52 (memory -> prompt, after the question: same statement slot 29% vs bridge alt's statement 9%, d3_main_ae_27b, UNVERIFIED) rests on 22 entities with one wording; D3b showed items of one entity are correlated, so its intervals were too narrow. If the slot answer holds with ~3x the entities, three wordings and entity-resampled intervals, the pointer reading is not an artefact of a few entities or one sentence frame; if it turns into "mixed" or "word", the README's D3 line must change.

hypotheses.H-pointer: memory -> prompt, after the question, window 44-52, pooled: verdict "same statement slot" (its cluster lower bound above the word's and the answer's upper bounds and the random push); same slot 20-35%; in >= 2 of 3 topics; named -> prompt shows it too; memory -> memory same slot <= 5%
hypotheses.H-word: verdict "bridge alt's statement" pooled (the word beats the slot once entities and wordings vary)
hypotheses.H-mixed: no outcome separates under entity-cluster intervals (pooled verdict "mixed"), or the verdict holds in fewer than 2 of 3 topics (topic-dependent)
hypotheses.H-value: the alt prompt's own answer already wins inside 44-52 (> 30% at layer 50 after the question)
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-pointer 0.35, H-mixed 0.35, H-word 0.2, H-value 0.1 (pointer_v2's offset run, scored by the coordinator: last two tokens, layer 50, same slot 28% vs bridge alt's statement ~32%, after the question layer 48 17% vs 26%, so the slot-over-word margin may not survive).

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring: "Decision rule" and "pointer_v4 additions"; the manifest records ci = entity_cluster). Per cell (family x patched tokens x layer or window x alt prompt), pooled over topics: interpretable iff the patch changes the answer (lower bound >= 0.20) and the same-entity control changes it rarely (upper bound <= 0.10); the verdict is the outcome among {bridge alt's statement, same statement slot, the alt prompt's own answer} whose lower bound exceeds the others' upper bounds, the random push's upper bound and the per-digit context rate; else "mixed". Every bound is the entity-cluster bootstrap 95% interval (asked entity resampled within each topic, 2000 resamples, seed 0) widened to Wilson where Wilson is wider. Primary: memory -> prompt, after the question, window 44-52. Secondary, reported not decisive: last two tokens, every single layer, per topic (a verdict holding in fewer than 2 of 3 topics is topic-dependent), per slot class, named -> prompt and memory -> memory. Every cut needs n >= 35.
controls: same entity, statements reshuffled (every hypothesis predicts answer org): damage bar
random push of the same size per token (layers 16, 32, 44, 48, 52): chance bar for each predicted digit
a prompt of another topic, same size: realistic-activation null
context digits no hypothesis predicts: per-digit chance
org prompt into itself (no-op) and the layer-0 all-position patch (hook checks; run invalid below 100%)
entity-cluster intervals: the effect must hold across entities, not within a few
n: 150 scenes per topic eligible in all three families (seed 0) x 3 topics x 3 families = 1,350 cases; per pooled cell 450 items over ~70-100 asked entities and 9 wordings; per topic 150 (>= 35 for every topic and slot cut). If a topic has fewer than 150 eligible scenes, all of them.
