title: D2 batch 3: which late attention heads (layers 51-63) read the answer's statement at the last tokens, and does one head's attention point at the asked statement?
command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name d2_lookup_heads --why "D2 batch 3 (a): one attention head at a time blocked from reading the answer's statement on pointer_v1 (animals, elements): late layers at the last tokens (memory → prompt, named → prompt), early layers at the question words (named → prompt), middle layers at question words and last tokens together (memory → prompt); memory → memory as the null; per-head attention to each statement saved (pointer readout)" --dataset pointer_v1 --families RL DL RR --domains animals elements --n 100 --competence d3b_competence_400 --grid heads --head-ranges late && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name d2_lookup_heads && uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py summarise --name d2_lookup_heads
examples_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name d2_lookup_heads --k 3
figures_command: uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py figures --name d2_lookup_heads
question: Batch 2 found three reads of the answer's statement in pointer_v1's locker scenes, all through attention (UNVERIFIED): (1) the last tokens read it late (layers 48-63) in memory → prompt; (2) in named → prompt the question words read it early (hiding it from the question words + last tokens in layers 0-31 leaves 1/175 right, attention layers only 6/175, DeltaNet layers only 175/175; the last tokens alone at 0-31 keep 175/175); (3) in memory → prompt the question words and the last tokens together in layers 32-47 (78/175 left, each alone 87-88%). Which attention heads do each read: one or a few query heads, one key/value group, one layer, or only all of them together? And does any single head's attention pattern point at the asked statement (a pointer readout better than D3b's slot probe, 39%)?
why_it_matters: A named head (or group) that reads the answer's statement is a concrete mechanism to check against the J-lens: if the late read sits in one head, D3's pointer can be traced to that head's query (what it asks for) and value (what it moves); if it is spread over every head and layer, single-head circuits are the wrong unit and the write-up should say "attention, redundantly". The early named → prompt read and the middle joint read of memory → prompt tell whether the recalled bridge uses the same heads as a named entity does, at a different depth.

hypotheses.H_reproduce: memory → prompt, every head of the 4 late attention layers (51, 55, 59, 63) blocked at the last tokens: answer org kept in 11-20% (the entity-cluster interval overlaps 11-20%), reproducing batch 2. Prior 0.7
hypotheses.H_late_few_heads: memory → prompt: no single late query head is a reader (24 heads x 4 layers; the read is redundant across heads), but at least one whole late layer is. Prior 0.45
hypotheses.H_named_early: named → prompt, every head of the 8 early attention layers (3, 7, ..., 31) blocked at the question words: <= 10% kept; and at least one single early head is a reader (a name-matching head). Prior 0.5 (<= 10% alone: 0.7)
hypotheses.H_name_tokens: named → prompt, early layers: blocking the read from the name tokens only (" pig") keeps answer org within 10 points of blocking it from all the question words, so the per-head results at the question words are about the name. Prior 0.6
hypotheses.H_mid_joint: memory → prompt, every head of the 4 middle attention layers (35, 39, 43, 47) blocked at the question words and the last tokens together: 30-60% kept (batch 2: 45% with the DeltaNet layers blocked too, which alone cost nothing), and no single middle head is a reader. Prior 0.5
hypotheses.H_readout: the late head chosen on even-numbered scenes looks most at the asked statement (attention from the last token, argmax over the 5 statements) on > 39% of odd-numbered scenes (entity-cluster lower bound > 39%, the D3b probe; chance 20%). Prior 0.7
hypotheses.H_null: memory → memory: every whole-layer and whole-range cell >= 95%. Prior 0.9

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/attn_knockout.py BATCH3_RULES and INTERVALS, written into manifest.json "batch3_rules" and "intervals"). Items: pointer_v1 main, animals and elements (every family passes d3b_competence_400's gate: clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85), scenes with every competence prompt right in all three families, first 100 per domain by scene id (they include all 175 items of d2_pointer_late_read), and unedited read right. Unit = one query head (Qwen3.6-27B: 24 query heads share 4 key/value heads, 6 per group; blocking a query head masks its scores only, its key/value partners still read), one key/value group (its 6 query heads), one layer (all heads), or the whole range. A unit is a READER if acc(control) - acc(unit) >= 10 points and the 95% entity-cluster bootstrap lower bound of that drop >= 5 points (control: the same unit blocked from a same-kind statement off the answer's path, same items). Intervals: entity-cluster bootstrap (the queried entities resampled within domain: 16 animals, 6 elements; 4,000 draws, seed 0) first, item-level Wilson / paired item bootstrap second; every number per domain with n items / k entities. Readout: the best head chosen on even-numbered scenes (pooled over memory → prompt and named → prompt), scored on odd-numbered ones; above the probe iff its entity-cluster lower bound > 39%. A single-head reader is read with its group and layer cells, never alone (480 single-head cells are tested: named → prompt 192 early + 96 late, memory → prompt 96 middle + 96 late; the report counts the rule's mirror image as a noise floor). n per cut: 100 per domain (>= 35).
controls: the same unit blocked from a statement of the same kind off the answer's path (another entity's locker, same token length, seeded per scene): every reader is measured against it
memory → memory on the same scenes (the answer is recalled; its "asked statement" is not needed): whole layers and whole ranges

the whole range (all heads of all its layers) as the reproduction of batch 2 (late: 11-20%; early: the question words + last tokens at 0-31, attention only, kept 6/175; middle: the joint block 78/175 with DeltaNet layers too)
the readout: the head is chosen on half the scenes and scored on the other half; chance (1 of 5 statements) 20%
pre-run check (check.json): an empty source leaves the answer read bit-exact; the per-head mask matches a naive fp64 reference (tests/test_knockout.py)
n: 200 org prompts per family (100 animals with 16 queried entities + 100 elements with 6; 392 / 337 scenes eligible)
notes: Split before the run (2026-10-21): this job runs the late range only (--head-ranges late, ~0.45 h; hypotheses H_reproduce, H_late_few_heads, H_readout, H_null); the early and middle ranges (H_named_early, H_name_tokens, H_mid_joint) run as d2_lookup_heads_early_mid with the same rule. The full design: Rows: 244,800 knocked reads: named → prompt 718 per item (early 8 layers x (24 heads + 4 groups + 1 layer) + the range = 233 units, + 9 name-token units; late 4 x 29 + 1 = 117 units; x 2 sources), memory → prompt 468 (middle 117 + late 117 units, x 2), memory → memory 38 (whole layers and ranges: 19 units x 2). At the measured 31-37 edited reads/s on ~80-token prompts: ~2.0 h + load, check and the attention readout ~0.2 h. Split if wall-clock matters: the same command with --head-ranges late (~0.45 h) and, under another name, --head-ranges early mid (~1.7 h). Local 0.8B CPU smoke (qwen35_08b_smoke_d2_heads_cpu3, 2 scenes per domain, --no-eligibility; the 0.8B's ranges: early 3-11, middle 15, late 19-23): every stage ran, check.json gates exact (no-op 0.0, positive control 0.0). Results: results/attn_knockout/d2_lookup_heads/.

question: With the prompts as plain text (no chat template: the statements, the question and the instruction, a newline and "Answer:"), when the alt prompt's hidden states at the last two tokens (":" and the read's space) are patched into the org prompt at layers 48-52, does the org prompt still answer the digit at the same statement slot more often than the digit of bridge alt's statement, as it does in chat format (layer 50: 50% vs 21%, d3v4_swap_main, UNVERIFIED)?
why_it_matters: G1 threat: every D2/D3 result reads the statement at the tokens after the question, which in chat format are mostly the chat template's tokens. title: D5a: after a patch moves the lookup to another statement, does the late head (layer 51, head 22) look at the new statement? (and the J-lens's word, on the same tokens)
command: uv run python scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py manifest --name d5a_head_pointer_27b --why "D5a task b: does layer 51 head 22 (and the next 4 late heads) follow the pointer when pointer_swap's alt patch at layers 48 / 50 moves the answer, on d3v4_swap_main's pointer_v4 scenes; the J-lens's word read on the same tokens" --n 150 --families RL DL RR --competence d3v4_competence_27b && uv run python scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py run --name d5a_head_pointer_27b && uv run python scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py summarise --name d5a_head_pointer_27b
examples_command: uv run python scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py examples --name d5a_head_pointer_27b --k 3
figures_command: uv run python scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py figures --name d5a_head_pointer_27b
question: On unedited scenes layer 51 head 22 looks most at the asked statement from the last token (100% of held-out pointer_v1 scenes), but also on recall questions (95%), where the statement is not needed (d2_lookup_heads, UNVERIFIED). D3's patch of the alt prompt's last tokens / tokens after the question at layers 48 or 50 moves the answer to another statement of the org prompt (to the statement at the alt prompt's slot, or the alt entity's). Item by item: after the patch, does the head look most at the statement the new answer comes from (it follows the pointer), or still at the org prompt's asked statement (it tracks something the patch does not change)? Is that better than the J-lens's word read on the same tokens?
why_it_matters: D5a asks for a pointer read-out next to the J-lens, which reads the word but not the pointer. A head whose attention follows the patched pointer item by item would be that read-out (one head's attention, no fit) and would place the pointer in the head's query at layer 51; a head that stays on the asked statement would mean its 100% on unedited scenes reflects the bridge's identity or position in the context, not the lookup in progress. The recall control separates the two: there the answer moves without any lookup.

hypotheses.H_head_follows: memory → prompt, layer 51 head 22: on rows whose answer moved to another statement it looks most at the new answer's statement (entity-cluster lower bound >= 60%), and on rows whose answer stayed at the asked statement (lower bound >= 80%). Prior 0.5
hypotheses.H_head_static: it stays on the asked statement when the answer moves (lower bound >= 60%). Prior 0.35
hypotheses.H_head_beats_lens: on the same moved rows the head names the new statement more often than the J-lens's top entity at the last token (layer 50, what the head reads): paired entity-cluster lower bound > 0. Prior 0.6
hypotheses.H_controls: the same-entity patch and the random push change <= 10% of answers in each lookup family (d3v4_swap_main: 0% [0, 1] for both). Prior 0.9

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/d5a_head_pointer.py docstring "Decision rule", written into the manifest). Items: pointer_v4 main, d3v4_swap_main's scenes (pointer_swap.sample_cases, seed 0, n=150 per topic, eligible in every family by d3v4_competence_27b): countries, animals, body (85 queried entities, 9 wordings), families memory → prompt (primary), named → prompt (reference), memory → memory (recall control). Edits per item: the org prompt's block output at the last two tokens, or at every token after the question, replaced at layer 48 or at layer 50 by the alt prompt's (dissoc), the same-entity prompt's (same), or a random direction of the dissoc patch's per-position norm added (rand); one batched forward with the unedited row. Rows: per item and edit; outcome kept / slot / word / other statement / off the prompt by pointer_swap's role map; moved = slot, word or other statement, its new statement the org statement holding the new answer (memory → memory: the alt entity's statement). Reader: the statement with the most attention from the last token (summed over its tokens) for each listed head, recomputed from the edited forward; the J-lens: the top of the five entity tokens at the last token, block 50. Primary cut: memory → prompt, dissoc, the four settings pooled; intervals by entity cluster (queried entity resampled within topic, 4,000 draws, seed 0), Wilson second; judged only with >= 35 moved and >= 35 kept rows. H_head_follows: moved rows new statement lower bound >= 60% AND kept rows asked statement lower bound >= 80%. H_head_static: moved rows asked statement lower bound >= 60%. Else neither. The other 4 heads: the same numbers, no verdict.
controls: same-entity patch (the same entity at the same slot, the rest reshuffled): every hypothesis predicts no move; the head should stay on the asked statement
random push of the dissoc patch's per-position norm: no move
memory → memory (recall questions): the answer moves without a lookup; does the head move to the bridge's new statement anyway?
the J-lens's word read on the same tokens and rows (paired)
check.json: a self-patch (the org prompt's own state) leaves the logits unchanged; the answer roles agree with d3v4_swap_main on the same items and edits
n: 1,350 org prompts (150 scenes per topic x 3 topics x 3 families), 4 patch settings x 3 sources each; moved rows expected (d3v4_swap_main, memory → prompt): ~23% / 81% (last tokens, layer 48 / 50), ~35% / 32% (tokens after the question): ~770 moved rows of 1,800
notes: Forwards: per item one of 3 rows (org, alt, same-entity block outputs at 48 and 50) and one of 14 rows (the unedited row, a self-patch check and 12 edits); ~2,700 forwards on ~85-token prompts, ~8 min, + model and lens load ~5 min. Heads: 51:22 (pre-registered), then 59:3, 59:1, 55:23, 59:21: the next by the same read-out on d2_lookup_heads (pointer_v1 scenes, held out from pointer_v4). Local 0.8B CPU smoke (qwen35_08b_smoke_d5a_cpu1, scratchpad; heads 23:0 and 23:5, patch layers 18 / 19, lens layer 22): every stage ran, the self-patch exact (0.0). Results: results/d5a_head_pointer/d5a_head_pointer_27b/.

Primary cell per topic; general iff the same verdict holds in >= 2 of 3 topics. Secondary: last two tokens at layer 50 and after the question at 48, per topic.
controls: same entity, statements reshuffled (every hypothesis predicts answer org)
random push of the same size; another topic's prompt of the same size

question: On the batch-3 items (pointer_v1, animals and elements), at which single layers (28-52, tokens after the cue) is the recalled word "in transit" (the lens push no longer changes the recalled fact on memory → memory, while pasting the alt prompt still changes >= 50% of lookups), and does the lens push write the lookup there (C2's kill test)?

hypotheses.H-C2-killed: in some topic the lens push writes the lookup at >= 3x random (paired lower bound > 0, upper bound >= 10%) at a transit layer

Intervals: entity-cluster bootstrap 95% (queried entity within its topic) widened to Wilson. With 2 topics, "H-C2-transit" needs both testable and holding. question: D2's strongest claim so far (UNVERIFIED) is that in a lookup the last tokens read the answer's statement themselves, late (layers 48-63), through attention: memory → prompt keeps 11% with every attention layer blocked at the last tokens and 99% with every DeltaNet layer blocked. It rests on 22 entities (16 animals, 6 elements) and one wording. Does it hold in each of three topics (countries "The Japan file is in drawer 3.", animals "The eagle's locker is 9.", body parts "The chart on the ear is kept in folder 6."), across 85 queried entities and 9 wordings, for memory → prompt and named → prompt, with memory → memory untouched?
why_it_matters: Items of one entity are correlated, so batch 2's 175 prompts are worth about 22 entities. A claim to freeze needs entities and wordings, not more scenes of the same ones: pointer_v4 has 34-36 entities per topic for countries and animals (15 body parts) and 9 wordings each. If the attention read holds in every topic by entity cluster, D2's claim is general for this scene format; if one topic differs (e.g. body parts, a different object noun and statement length), the claim must be scoped.

hypotheses.H_general: memory → prompt, the statement giving the answer hidden from the last tokens in every attention layer: <= 20% kept, and in every DeltaNet layer: >= 90% kept, in each of the 3 topics (decided on the entity-cluster bounds; "point" if only the point estimates pass). Prior 0.7 (coordinator); agent: 0.75 on the point estimates, 0.45 on the bounds (pointer_v1 animals kept more than elements: 29% vs 8% with layers 48-63 hidden)
hypotheses.H_general_named: named → prompt: the same in each topic (batch 2: every attention layer 13%, every DeltaNet layer 100%). Prior 0.7
hypotheses.H_late_band_topics: memory → prompt, hidden from the last tokens in layers 48-63 only: <= 40% kept in each topic (point estimate; batch 2: 19%). Prior 0.7
hypotheses.H_named_question_topics: named → prompt, hidden from the question words in all layers: <= 10% kept in each topic (batch 2: 1%; the name reads its statement early). Prior 0.75
hypotheses.H_null_topics: memory → memory: every cell >= 95% in each topic. Prior 0.85
hypotheses.positive_control: every lookup family with the statement hidden from everything after it and removed from the DeltaNet recurrence: NEEDED (5 statements: guessing gives ~20%)

decision_rule: Fixed before the run (scripts/attn_knockout.py GENERAL, TOPIC_SETS, general_claim; the batch-2 rule in the manifest "decision"). Items: pointer_v4 main, topics countries, animals, body (every family passes d3v4_competence_27b's gate, clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85), scenes with every competence prompt right in all three families, first 100 per topic by scene id (they cover every queried entity: countries 36, animals 34, body 15, and all 9 wordings per topic), unedited read right. H_general per topic: memory → prompt, (statement giving the answer, last tokens, every attention layer) entity-cluster 95% upper bound <= 20% AND (same, every DeltaNet layer) entity-cluster lower bound >= 90% -> holds; both point estimates pass but a bound does not -> "point"; else fails. Over topics: holds if all hold, partly if none fails, else fails. Entity-cluster bootstrap: queried entities resampled within the topic, 4,000 draws, seed 0; the Wilson interval second; n items / k entities / t wordings per cell. The batch-2 cell rule (pooled over topics, item level) is kept for comparison: NEEDED if accuracy drops >= 20 points and the paired bootstrap 95% lower bound of acc(off-path statement) - acc(cell) >= 10 points; NOT NEEDED if the Wilson lower bound >= 90%; else PARTIAL. A family whose positive control is not NEEDED is not interpreted. n per cut: 100 per topic (body: 15 entities, so its entity-cluster intervals are the widest).

memory → memory on the same scenes (the answer is recalled; the statement is not needed)

pre-run check (check.json): an empty source leaves the answer read bit-exact; context independence under full blocking; an unedited row in every batch
n: 900 org prompts (100 scenes per topic x 3 families; 85 queried entities, 9 wordings per topic)
notes: Rows: 110,700 knocked reads (123 per item: 4 destinations x 4 sources in all layers, 2 x 4 with the statement removed from the recurrence, and 11 layer sets (every attention / DeltaNet layer; bands 0-31, 32-47, 48-63 whole, attention-only, DeltaNet-only) x 3 destinations (question words, last tokens, both) x 3 sources). why_it_matters: "The pointer is an order index counted from the start" rests on single layers of pointer_v2 / v3 runs with 22 entities and one wording, whose pre-registered cells (after the question, layers 44-52 together) read "alt answer" or "mixed" because the digit arrives by layer 52. hypotheses.H-text-position: the same token position beats order (filler moved) or both rivals beat the start: the pointer is an address in the token sequence
hypotheses.prior: Coordinator's priors: H-order-v4 0.6, H-start-v4 0.55.

title: D3b fair test of C2 on three topics: where the lens reads the word, does a pointer push steer the lookup the lens push cannot, and where is the word "in transit"?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fair.py run --data pointer_v4 --name d3b_fair_c2_v4 --competence d3v4_competence_27b --why "Batch 4, G2: the fair C2 test (pointer push vs lens push, same size, same target digit, layers 32-40, after the cue and at the question words, 1x and 2x) on pointer_v4 (countries, animals, body; fit on the fit set, push only items whose asked entity or wording the fit never saw), with the memory → memory control per topic; plus the transit sweep (layers 28-52 one at a time, after the cue, 1x and 4x: the lens push and the alt-prompt copy on memory → prompt, the lens push on memory → memory) that defines 'in transit' before C2's kill test"
examples_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fair.py examples --name d3b_fair_c2_v4
figures_command: uv run python scripts/pointer_fair.py figures --name d3b_fair_c2_v4
question: (1) At layers 32-40, on the tokens after the cue, does a pointer push toward bridge alt's statement switch memory → prompt answers to that statement's digit where the lens push of the same size, aimed at the same digit, does not, in at least 2 of 3 topics, without changing memory → memory answers? (2) For each topic, at which layers is the recalled word "in transit" (the lens push no longer changes the recalled fact on memory → memory, while pasting the alt prompt still changes >= 50% of lookups), and can the lens push write the lookup there (C2's kill test)?
why_it_matters: (1) The batch-3 fair test (pointer_v1) failed only through elements (6 entities; memory → memory changed 31% there, 2% in animals; animals alone: pointer 43% vs lens 7%), so the link "the lookup goes around the lens = a pointer at the depth where the lens reads but cannot write" is undecided. pointer_v4 has 15-36 asked entities per topic, 9 wordings and a recorded held-out split. (2) An outside review found the batch-3 run fires Zach's C2 kill test (elements, after the cue, 32-40, 1x: lens 30/150 vs random 2/150) while the lens push also wrote recall questions there (55/100): the word was still being recalled, so "in transit" has to be defined operationally before the test. If C2 holds in the transit layers, "read without write" is stated for the right layers; if the lens writes there, C2 is killed; if recall and copy overlap at every layer, C2 cannot be tested on these prompts.

hypotheses.H-pointer-at-lens-depth: after the cue, layers 32-40 at once, 1x: pointer entity-cluster lower bound >= 0.30, >= 20 points above the lens push (and the random push), memory → memory changed <= 0.10, in >= 2 of 3 topics
hypotheses.H-pointer-later-only: pointer < 15% at layers 32-40 in >= 2 topics (the pointer forms later, 44-50)
hypotheses.H-pointer-not-lookup-specific: memory → memory answers changed by the pointer push > 10% in >= 2 topics
hypotheses.H-C2-transit: transit layers exist in >= 2 of 3 topics and C2 holds there (lens on memory → prompt < 3x random or under 10% at every transit layer)
hypotheses.H-no-transit: in some topic the lens still writes the recall at every layer where the alt-prompt copy switches >= 50% of lookups (no transit layer)
hypotheses.H-C2-killed: in some topic the lens push writes the lookup at >= 3x random (paired lower bound > 0, upper bound >= 10%) at a transit layer
hypotheses.H-overshoot: secondary: the pointer push's off-target answers land beyond the target more often than a uniform choice, pooled and in >= 2 topics
hypotheses.prior: Agent prior: H-pointer-at-lens-depth 0.4, H-pointer-later-only 0.35, H-pointer-not-lookup-specific 0.25; H-C2-transit 0.55, H-no-transit 0.25, H-C2-killed 0.2; H-overshoot 0.6 if the pointer moves answers at all.

decision_rule: Fixed in scripts/pointer_fair.py's docstring ("pointer_v4 additions" and "transit sweep") and copied to the manifest. Intervals: entity-cluster bootstrap 95% (asked entity resampled within its topic, 2000, seed 0), widened to the item-level Wilson interval where wider; differences: cluster bootstrap of the per-item paired difference; n items / k entities / t wordings reported for every cell. (1) Deciding cell per topic: memory → prompt, after the cue ('?' and the 20 template tokens), layers 32, 36, 40 at once, 1x. A topic passes iff the pointer push's rate of answers = bridge alt's statement digit has a lower bound >= 0.30 and exceeds the lens push and the random push by >= 20 points, each paired lower bound > 0; it counts only if valid: the shuffled-label direction's rate and the share of memory → memory answers the pointer push changes (same topic and cell) both have an upper bound <= 0.10, n >= 35 each. The claim holds iff >= 2 of 3 topics pass and are valid. Flags: pointer only later (< 15% in >= 2 topics); not lookup-specific (memory → memory changed > 10% in >= 2 topics). The question words, 2x, single layers, topics pooled, per held-out cut: reported, not decisive (at the question words the pointer is the mean over the question's tokens, since their number differs between wordings). (2) Transit, per topic, at 1x (4x reported the same way): a single layer (28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48, 52; after the cue) is in transit iff the memory → memory lens rate (answers = bridge alt's recalled fact) has an upper bound <= 2x the memory → memory random rate's upper bound, and the alt-prompt copy changes >= 50% of memory → prompt answers. C2 at a transit layer holds iff the memory → prompt lens rate is < 3x the random rate or its upper bound < 0.10; else killed iff the paired lens − random lower bound > 0; else unclear. Topic: not testable (no transit layer), killed (any killed layer), holds (all hold), else undecided. Overshoot (secondary): off-target statement answers beyond the target vs a uniform choice, entity-cluster lower bound > 0, pooled and per topic.
controls: lens push bridge alt − bridge org at the same per-token size, aimed at the same digit (the comparison C2 is about)
random push per token at the same size (pointer arm and transit sweep, both families)
shuffled-label direction (statement labels permuted before the fit)
memory → memory items per topic: nothing is looked up, so a pointer should change nothing; in the sweep, where the lens still writes the recall

question: When the alt prompt's last two tokens are patched into the org prompt at layers 48-50, and one prompt has an extra sentence before its list (every statement moves in the text; its distance back from the question stays) or before its question (the distance back changes; the place in the text stays), which org statement does the answer come from: the same slot, the one at the same place in the text, or the one as far back from the question? And does the same-slot share drop with statements twice as long?
why_it_matters: pointer_v4x showed the address follows the order index rather than the place in the text; there the place in the text and the distance back from the question moved together. This run separates them. Dan's prediction: the relative shift (distance back) matters more, as rotary position encodes distances. If the slot survives both shifts, the address is an order index, not a token offset of either kind.

hypotheses.H-rel (Dan): share of answers at the same distance back (e5-rel) minus share at the same place in the text (e5-abs) has lower bound > 0 at layer 48 or 50 (memory -> prompt, last two tokens, pooled). Agents' prior 0.35
hypotheses.H-abs: the same difference has upper bound < 0. Prior 0.15
hypotheses.H-ordinal: in both shifted layouts the same slot's lower bound exceeds the moved statement's upper bound, at layer 48 or 50. Prior 0.6
hypotheses.H-long (Dan): same-slot share, long minus still, upper bound < 0 at layer 48 or 50. Prior 0.4

decision_rule: Fixed before the run: scripts/pointer_swap.py docstring, "pointer_v6 additions" (analyze writes the tests to summary.json `v6` and report.md). PRIMARY: memory -> prompt, the last two tokens, layers 48 and 50, pooled over topics; a hypothesis holds if its test passes at either layer with n >= 35 in both layouts compared. Differences: Newcombe 95% on items (the layouts share their scenes, so this is conservative); per-layout bounds: entity-cluster bootstrap widened to Wilson. The full rule's verdicts, per topic cells, named -> prompt, the tokens after the question and other layers are reported, not decisive. H-long's plain-answer half is d3v6_competence_27b's.
controls: same entity, statements reshuffled, the org layout (every hypothesis predicts answer org): damage bar
random push of the same size per token at every layer: chance bar for each predicted digit
a prompt of another topic, same size, aligned from the end: realistic-activation null
e5-still: the same scenes with nothing moved (the reference for both shifts and for long statements)
org prompt into itself (no-op); the layer-0 all-position check for the same-length layouts
n: up to 150 scenes per topic eligible in every layout and both families (seed 0) x 3 topics x 4 layouts x 2 families = up to 3,600 cases; per pooled primary cell up to 450 items over 85 entities and 27 wordings
notes: ~2.1 GPU-h (d3v4x_swap_main: 2,700 cases, 5 layers, 1.5 h). The e5-abs and e5-rel sources are one sentence longer or shorter than the org prompt; pointer_swap maps the patched positions from the end and checks that the question and the template tokens line up (prepare).

question: On OLMo-3-7B-Instruct (32 layers, softmax attention in each; 3 of 4 sliding-window, 4096 tokens), when the answer's statement is hidden from the last tokens, does a lookup in the prompt (memory -> prompt, named -> prompt) break while a recall (memory -> memory) does not, as on Qwen3.6-27B? In which 4-layer band must the statement stay visible?
why_it_matters: D2 ("the last tokens read the answer's statement late, through attention") rests on one hybrid model. OLMo has no DeltaNet layers, so the attention-vs-DeltaNet half cannot transfer, but the late read can: if it is there, and in the layers just after OLMo's slot phase (17-19), the lookup's last step is a property of transformers' in-context lookups, not of Qwen3.6-27B.

hypotheses.H-late-read: statement hidden from the last tokens in every layer: memory -> prompt still right <= 20% (upper bound) pooled, memory -> memory >= 90% (lower bound). Prior 0.7
hypotheses.H-band: the band whose blocking alone breaks memory -> prompt most lies at or after layer 16 (the last third or the 4-layer bands 16-27). Prior 0.6

decision_rule: attn_knockout's rule as in d2_v4_late_read (kept = the unedited answer survives the block; entity-cluster intervals; the off-path same-length control and the random-span control must keep >= 90%). PRIMARY: memory -> prompt, statement hidden from the tokens after the question in all layers, pooled over topics. Bands, topics, named -> prompt and the question words are reported.
controls: off-path: another statement of the same length hidden (should keep the answer)
random span of the same length hidden
memory -> memory: the answer is recalled, so hiding the statement should not matter
n: 100 items per family (eligible in olmo3_7b_instruct_d3v4_competence), 3 topics
notes: ~0.6 GPU-h on one A100 (7B; the 27B grid took 1.1 h with more layer sets).

hypotheses.H-lookup-survives: prompt -> prompt and memory -> prompt (whole question): accuracy with the J-space removed >= 90% and within 10 points of the rotated control. Prior 0.7
hypotheses.H-recall-drops: prompt -> memory and memory -> memory: accuracy with the J-space removed <= 60% while the rotated control keeps >= 90% (late layers: the recalled answer may already be formed, so this may fail). Prior 0.35

decision_rule: Per family (whole question, "clean"), accuracy under none / J-space removed / rotated removal (same norm per position), Wilson 95% on items. H-lookup-survives: both lookup families' J-space accuracy lower bound >= 0.85 and point within 10 points of rotated. H-recall-drops: both recall families' J-space upper bound <= 0.60 and rotated lower bound >= 0.85. The last step alone ("hop") and the countries set are reported.
controls: rotated: the J-space fit turned by a fixed random rotation (the same norm removed, position by position)
the last step alone (hop): what each family loses without the first hop
n: 100 eligible items per family (animal suite, competence_v2), countries from map_v1
notes: One band per job, so a band whose lens map is missing fails alone. abl_rot_v1 is the same at 32 36 40.

question: On Qwen3.5-9B (32 layers: 8 attention, 24 DeltaNet), at the layers where the alt prompt's digit has not yet arrived at the last tokens, does patching the alt prompt's last two tokens give the digit of the same statement slot more often than bridge alt's statement and the alt digit, as on the 27B?
why_it_matters: The README's pattern 5 is shown on one model; OLMo tests another architecture. A smaller model of the same family says whether the statement address comes with this family's design at another size.

title: D3b mechanism: is the fitted slot direction the model's own statement address, or just a direction that moves the answer?
command: uv run python scripts/pointer_mechanism.py run --name d3b_mechanism_smoke_27b --n-test 2 --rr-n 1 --why "smoke: the six tests on 2 scenes per topic; not a result" && uv run python scripts/pointer_mechanism.py run --name d3b_mechanism_27b --n-test 150 --rr-n 50 --why "D3b mechanism (22 Oct): ordered axis, dose path through the slots in between, natural dose, necessity (remove the 4-dim slot subspace), the late head as the reader, ordinal words; held-out pointer_v4 items, layer 48"
question: The slot direction moves the lookup where random, shuffled and lens directions of the same norm do not. Is it the model's own address? (1) Are the five slot means ordered on an axis? (2) Pushing from slot a toward slot j, does the answer pass through the slots in between? (3) Does it steer at its natural size (mu_j - mu_a), not only at a patch's norm? (4) Does removing the 4-dim slot subspace break the lookup but not recall? (5) Does the late head 51/22 follow the push? (6) Is the slot code like the words "first", "2", "three"?
why_it_matters: pointer_fit shows sufficiency of a direction at a matched norm. A direction can move an answer without being what the model uses (an off-manifold push, a label-specific shortcut). Necessity, natural size, an ordered geometry and a reader that follows the push would make "the lookup runs on a statement address" a mechanism, not a steering trick.

hypotheses.H-axis: class-mean distances grow with |i - j|: Spearman rho >= 0.8 at layer 48, label-permutation p < 0.05. Prior 0.6
hypotheses.H-path: on the dose path from a toward j (|j - a| >= 2) the first statement reached is in between more often than chance, rarely on the other side. Prior 0.4
hypotheses.H-jump: the path jumps straight to j (>= 50%) with no excess of in-between slots. Prior 0.3
hypotheses.H-natural: at its natural size (alpha 1 or 2) the slot push moves >= 10% (lower bound) to j, above random. Prior 0.5
hypotheses.H-necessary: removing the 4-dim slot subspace at the tokens after the question (layers 44-52) leaves memory -> prompt <= 70% right, >= 20 points below random and top-variance removals, with memory -> memory >= 90%. Prior 0.3
hypotheses.H-reader: on alpha-2 pushes that moved the answer to j, head 51/22 looks most at statement j on >= 50%. Prior 0.55

decision_rule: Fixed before the run in scripts/pointer_mechanism.py's docstring ("Decision rule"); analyze writes summary.json with each hypothesis holds / does not hold. Held-out pointer_v4 items only (asked entity or wording outside the fit), memory -> prompt primary, memory -> memory the control; layer 48 primary for the pushes; removals at every layer 44-52.
controls: label-permutation null for the axis (200 shuffles)
random direction of the same per-token norm as the natural push
removal of a random 4-dim subspace and of the top-4 directions of overall variance (same operation)
memory -> memory items: removal should not matter
random tokens for the word comparison
n: 150 memory -> prompt and 50 memory -> memory held-out items per topic (3 topics); the fit set for the means
notes: ~0.8 GPU-h; the smoke runs first in the same command.

title: Name vs digit: what do the question's tokens and the last tokens take from the answer's statement? (Qwen3-32B)
command: BJ_TARGET=qwen3-32b uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py manifest --name qwen3_32b_d2_parts --dataset pointer_v4 --families RL DL --n 100 --sources lookup lookup_off lookup_name lookup_digit lookup_off_name lookup_off_digit --dests question final --layers all --competence qwen3_32b_d3v4_competence_r2 --why "D2 follow-up (name vs digit): hide only the entity's name or only the digit of the answer's statement (and of an off-path statement) from the question's tokens or from the last tokens, in every layer; analysed by scripts/d2_parts.py" && BJ_TARGET=qwen3-32b uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py run --name qwen3_32b_d2_parts
examples_command: BJ_TARGET=qwen3-32b uv run python scripts/attn_knockout.py examples --name qwen3_32b_d2_parts --k 3
figures_command: uv run python scripts/d2_parts.py --name qwen3_32b_d2_parts
question: When only the entity's name, or only the digit, of the answer's statement is hidden from the question's tokens or from the last tokens, how many lookups stay right, and where do the wrong answers go?
why_it_matters: Qwen3-32B: 32% right without the statement at the question's tokens. Hiding the whole statement from the question's tokens breaks lookups on Qwen3-32B, OLMo and Qwen3.5-9B with mostly off-list answers: the question's tokens take something other than the digit choice from the statement, perhaps the name to resolve the bridge. The last tokens should need the digit.

hypotheses.H-name-q: where the question needs the statement at all (whole statement hidden from the question leaves <= 0.70 right): hiding the name alone there hurts as much as the whole statement (within 0.15) and the digit alone keeps >= 0.85. Prior 0.55
hypotheses.H-digit-final: from the last tokens, hiding the digit alone leaves <= 0.35 right and the name alone >= 0.70. Prior 0.6

decision_rule: scripts/d2_parts.py (committed before this run): memory -> prompt, topics pooled, items right unedited; valid iff the off-path name and digit controls keep >= 0.90 right at both destinations; question hypotheses testable iff the whole statement hidden from the question leaves <= 0.70 right; H-name-q, H-digit-q, H-digit-final, H-name-final as in its docstring. Error types (another list digit vs off the list) reported for every cell.
controls: the same parts (name, digit) of an off-path statement of the same length; the whole statement and the whole off-path statement
n: 100 items per family, 3 topics (pointer_v4)
notes: Qwen3-32B: 32% right without the statement at the question's tokens. Not opened before Dan predicts (batch 8).
